| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | I’ve known Reed Olson for about 20 years. He’s a good citizen of Bemidji and I admired his intelligence and educated perspective, and votes, on issues while on both the Bemidji City Council and the Beltrami County Board. Besides those responsibilities he also owns a restaurant and I worked with him and others to open two Bemidji facilities to provide services for the homeless. Reed knows how governing works, he’s open-minded and pragmatic. We very much need him to represent us in the legislature and for Pete’s sake people, he’s an Olson. How much more Minnesotan is that?
_Kristi Tell Miller_ Retired Bemidji-ite

I hope you're having a good day. I'm writing with some exciting news.
[](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckUuOnDAQQE9jdiD_ms-CRSIgmijTUcIiS8ttF1CSsS1seq4fIfVcYBa1eU96JVX9e1fvGh369a536DElZYNVeYMDnM4YfNowPiB_APg1WMUpr0tGS14rbTI-QUld2P7GWbu0BfSs6QRlNee82Pobq6ls2KM1tLvYrdWStgA3xngrm6XA_uqxazgVoqkenaw708i2fXRWLJRIekarM1ToE1pIJoQYg8OMJlXhWAvXbznHRMQ3wifCJ_RLqDZ0LlntoAJ7Ej6VK3hImMrlACjt05ZhWeAgYkqGiIHSTtZ3yiX_9fP78HsYx5nw-sy7SuE8DBAxxCOkCCajX19qB4vnTsQAu0b3gkbvUePqiRheK5V92k8ZfAafiRh-jPdxfpunv-Oo_jTl2zyXn4cojt7GD3QOU90QSderXpmwF_mr73n2_H8AAAD__5RVnoc)
Hillsdale College's popular online course, **" The Genesis Story: Reading Biblical Narratives,"** is now FREE on DVD.

In this six-lecture course, you'll explore some of the major themes of Genesis, including the complex relationship between God and man, and what it reveals about divine and human nature.

"The Genesis Story" is taught by Hillsdale College professor of English Justin Jackson, who has taught the subject to undergraduate students here at the College for 15 years. This course aims to deepen a student's theological understanding of the Old Testament by revealing the literary beauty and complexity of the text.

The course begins with a lecture and introduction by the president of Hillsdale College, Larry P. Arnn, in which he explains why we teach the Book of Genesis at Hillsdale College and why it's important to both faith and higher education.

Then, Dr. Jackson explains the four relationships that dominate the Book of Genesis: God and creation, God and man, man and man, and man and creation.

You'll explore these relationships in the narratives of Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Abraham and Isaac, Jacob and Esau, and finally, Joseph.

This course on DVD is perfect for viewing in your home with your family or for use in small groups such as Bible studies and book clubs.

**To receive your FREE Genesis DVD box set, please use the secure link here:**[https://info.hillsdale.edu/-genesis-free-dvd-offer](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckUuOnDAQQE9jdiD_ms-CRSIgmijTUcIiS8ttF1CSsS1seq4fIfVcYBa1eU96JVX9e1fvGh369a536DElZYNVeYMDnM4YfNowPiB_APg1WMUpr0tGS14rbTI-QUld2P7GWbu0BfSs6QRlNee82Pobq6ls2KM1tLvYrdWStgA3xngrm6XA_uqxazgVoqkenaw708i2fXRWLJRIekarM1ToE1pIJoQYg8OMJlXhWAvXbznHRMQ3wifCJ_RLqDZ0LlntoAJ7Ej6VK3hImMrlACjt05ZhWeAgYkqGiIHSTtZ3yiX_9fP78HsYx5nw-sy7SuE8DBAxxCOkCCajX19qB4vnTsQAu0b3gkbvUePqiRheK5V92k8ZfAafiRh-jPdxfpunv-Oo_jTl2zyXn4cojt7GD3QOU90QSderXpmwF_mr73n2_H8AAAD__5RVnoc)

Warm regards,

Bill Gray, '01

In case you missed it, October has become a terrible time for people who imagine our systems to be secure from AI. Major banks [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/d3b5e016-846f-4c5f-9526-449b5bd9fbf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that AI agents were messing around in customer accounts. I'd heard from a friend that the CEO of one of them was calling Anthropic freaked out about his inability to safeguard consumers from bots. Quest Diagnostics [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/c9f6fe12-0971-4153-9ca2-1b25f83a2db0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a hack that could affect millions of patients, as they serve roughly half of U.S. hospitals and physicians.
Roughly 3% of all critical software security bugs ever officially logged in history were [discovered](https://substack.com/redirect/1c06ce69-6c39-4ba3-bde2-b92b04edb71a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in October to date, driven largely by the use of AI models to scan open-source codebases like PHP. "In the last 2 days there have been several dozen cyber attacks which, in isolation, would each have been the worst to happen in an entire calendar year," tech expert John Milinovich [writes](https://substack.com/redirect/210a838f-49ba-43a3-bf99-fcd97ef93e84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "Every sector from government to education to big tech and banks is being massively affected . . . in a nutshell, what's happened is that frontier AI models have gotten to the point where they are as advanced as the most sophisticated programmers . . . [open source models] are being used by black hat hackers to wreak havoc . . . the societal and individual risk is very real, and is playing out NOW."
Someone [hacked refrigerators](https://substack.com/redirect/b0bf3d16-af75-45ea-a109-6b8c978c8ec4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in French supermarkets and set them to defrost, spoiling tons of food. Why? Who? No one knows. John recommends setting up 2-factor authentication and a password manager as quickly as possible as your data has probably been hacked somewhere.
I talked to someone who works in cybersecurity this weekend. He said, "Everyone is putting in late nights. But there are a lot of apps and websites that aren't updated or well-maintained. That's a ton of holes and vulnerabilities."
Yes, it's time to change your passwords.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fde5ff38-d78d-44c0-9ef7-04347a8f1618?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The hacking of our digital and real world infrastructure has always been a massive concern for me; it's a lot easier for the bad guys to play offense in this realm than for the good guys to play defense; playing defense involves patching bugs and holes in decades-old systems that were never designed with the future in mind. Do you think that the manufacturers of freezers in France years ago ever thought that their software would need to guard against malignant hackers trying to turn them off just to screw with people? AI is a set of ultrapowerful tools, and there are some very bad actors out there.
Tech stocks [dipped](https://substack.com/redirect/2e443c57-a71a-45a6-9e6c-7db661739288?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday as people started to recalibrate on the risk/reward to AI development, which includes the prospect of hundreds of billions of dollars being spent on data centers and infrastructure with an unclear timeline for it to pay off. They recovered on Friday, but I'd expect a lot of volatility upcoming, in both the markets and in the real world. "I think websites and services are just going to be randomly shut down for various periods for the next 18 months due to our inability to insulate the Internet from hackers," is what one expert predicts.
All of the above is going to make people very angry. After all, what good is AI if we are all in the Stone Age unable to access our bank accounts or even have power because our grid is being hacked all of the time?
Take precautions in your own life: hide some cash in the mattress, write down a new password on a piece of paper, and try to imagine a world where bot swarms are trying to steal your info online at every turn. Because unfortunately, that future has arrived.
I'm on the way to South Dakota for [Brian Bengs](https://substack.com/redirect/89035ea0-ab4f-44ea-a407-732b280471a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who is running for U.S. Senate and is tied with the incumbent Mike Rounds. Please consider donating to [Brian Bengs](https://substack.com/redirect/89035ea0-ab4f-44ea-a407-732b280471a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Todd Achilles](https://substack.com/redirect/1012b6cd-177b-4b19-ade4-726f17a46ece?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and/or [Seth Bodnar](https://substack.com/redirect/85603a4b-be1a-4543-8f8c-e8bd0cd1c05a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), or to [Forward](https://substack.com/redirect/128a96f5-37d3-413a-8616-1aac92b7c863?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) which is sending people with me to South Dakota. Imagine 1 or 2 senators who don't owe fealty to either party establishment - they could change everything. I discuss his new [book](https://substack.com/redirect/05e635f2-6d5a-4563-9e30-0700a3a3bc48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "A World We Share: Hannah Arendt and the Power of Friendship," with Roger Berkowitz this week on the [podcast](https://substack.com/redirect/0be5470c-b9a6-4453-8762-7a983e5c2fa5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). # [My Voters Didn't Change. The Lines Did.](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2841627&post_id=222033543&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIyMDMzNTQzLCJpYXQiOjE3OTMwMTcxMTUsImV4cCI6MTc5NTYwOTExNSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI4NDE2MjciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.yh1b9MkdY-8Ciynh0itIHTZIUg6M7GyhXF_qEW8XELM)
### The AP just told the story of my old congressional district. It's also the story of why Congress is so broken.
| | [Congressman Wiley Nickel](https://substack.com/@wileynickel)
---

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/880d3548-65b3-4858-990c-153f1941e1c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In 2022, I won North Carolina's 13th Congressional District by about 9,000 votes. It was one of the last real swing districts in the South and one of only six nationwide to flip from red to blue. To win it, I had to earn votes from Democrats, Republicans and unaffiliated voters. That's what a competitive seat does. It means you have to listen to everybody.
Then the Republican legislature redrew the map.
[The AP just wrote a big story about it and laid out what they did](https://substack.com/redirect/80aa7c7f-ff6e-4545-80c6-116507218747?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). They took a district shaped like a rectangle and turned it into one shaped like a monster eating Wake County. They cut out Democratic voters in Raleigh and swapped in rural counties stretching up to the Virginia border. In 2024, the Republican candidate won it by more than 70,000 votes.
Same district. Two years apart. The voters didn't change. The lines did.
#### **Then Trump came back for more**
Last fall, Trump told Republicans to draw another Republican seat in North Carolina. House Speaker Destin Hall said they'd stand with the president, defend the GOP majority and secure an additional Republican congressional seat. Trump went on Truth Social and urged North Carolina Republican legislators to work as hard as they could to [pass the new map](https://substack.com/redirect/88932b64-be72-41c6-b106-52eadddecf58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
They didn't even pretend it was about anything else. Republican State Sen. Ralph Hise, [who helped lead the gerrymandering effort](https://substack.com/redirect/0a57e43c-1a23-4c69-91e5-ec89b0f2bd30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), said, "_The motivation behind this redraw is simple and singular: Draw a new map that will bring an additional Republican seat to the North Carolina congressional delegation._ "
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ca1d267e-4a0e-4591-9630-d7243bda088e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The target was Rep. Don Davis in eastern North Carolina. [Under the new lines](https://substack.com/redirect/ca1d267e-4a0e-4591-9630-d7243bda088e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Trump would have carried the 1st District by 12 points.
Trump leaned on Republican state legislators to pick his voters for him because he knew they couldn't win without cheating.
#### **It 's backfiring on Republicans**
Here's the part they didn't plan for. Voters in Eastern NC don't like being gerrymandered. Don Davis' district, redrawn to favor Republicans as part of Trump's mid-decade gerrymandering push, is now [rated a toss-up](https://substack.com/redirect/4dd429cb-87ab-404e-a2a9-5911bdf14fe9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the Cook Political Report.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1eec9972-c8d0-421d-a7a2-1bc0ae405b73?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It's happening in other recently gerrymandered states too:
* **Texas:** Cook just moved Texas' 34th District to Lean Democratic, and the 35th, which Republicans redrew to cut out Austin, [is now a toss-up](https://substack.com/redirect/a396d779-40d1-440c-9aab-9445b8c11e44?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **Ohio and Florida:** Republicans redrew Rep. Greg Landsman's and Rep. Jared Moskowitz's districts hoping to flip them, and Cook has since [moved both further toward Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/fe96e71c-3b68-4a8b-a3b8-d9806b868376?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Cook's David Wasserman says that Republicans are falling short of the 10 to 12 seats their strategists first expected to gain from 2025 redistricting, and Cook now projects the likeliest outcome is a net GOP gain of around three seats from redistricting alone, with Democrats strongly favored to win the House. As of this week, Cook has Democrats favored in 220 seats, Republicans in 198, and 17 toss-ups. We only need 218 to elect a Speaker - trust me I know. I've voted for Speaker 19 times when I was in the House.
Why? It's no secret. Donald Trump is driving all of this. [He told voters to pretend he's on the ballot.](https://substack.com/redirect/913c66bf-40e3-425b-8271-34a46102d05b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Well, they are. They're voting against the most corrupt administration in American history. They're voting against a guy who promised to bring prices down and instead made life much more expensive for everyone. And they're voting against his war of choice with Iran, a forever war he dragged us into without ever making the case to Congress or the American people.
This is what a really bad year looks like for Trump. Most of the seats the Republicans gerrymandered for Trump are still in play.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4a881f22-acd3-43e1-88ff-d99ffc7aaedf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And the new 13th District? It's looking a little less safe right now. The Cook Political Report moved NC-13 from Solid Republican to Likely Republican. That's a big deal in a district drawn to never be competitive. And it's not just here. Cook moved 19 House races toward Democrats in a single day.
Want to track it yourself? The Cook Report keeps a free [redistricting map](https://substack.com/redirect/39d502e3-5c35-4f33-a06b-9debd92410b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [race ratings](https://substack.com/redirect/4a881f22-acd3-43e1-88ff-d99ffc7aaedf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) page.
#### **Why this matters to you**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ee1aea05-2f78-4763-a193-32aabd756b50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
When a seat is safe, the only election that counts is the primary. 90% of members of Congress are incentivized only to answer to the loudest slice of their own party, not to voters in November.
I told the [AP](https://substack.com/redirect/80aa7c7f-ff6e-4545-80c6-116507218747?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the biggest divide I found in Congress wasn't Democrat versus Republican. It was safe seats versus competitive seats. When you have to earn every voter's support, you think differently. You focus on solving real problems, and you've got every reason to work across the aisle. That's why I still believe the answer is independent redistricting commissions, like the ones in the [FAIR MAPS Act](https://substack.com/redirect/914de579-92db-484a-8e98-6d65d14ae6fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) I introduced in Congress.
#### **The last word**
I'm on the ballot this year for Wake County District Attorney, and I'm running unopposed in the general election. While I'm grateful for every voter who continues to vote for me - I knew that as soon as I voted for myself the election was over. That's its own little lesson in how sorted we've become. Republicans didn't even bother to field a candidate for District Attorney in Wake County.
Now gerrymandering makes winning harder. But it doesn't make your vote meaningless. On November 3rd, the voters get the last word. Make sure you're one of them.
Find your polling place and registration info at [iwillvote.com](https://substack.com/redirect/69825642-43d9-4b7e-ab3f-3c0e48284bc6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Wiley
[DONATE TODAY](https://substack.com/redirect/ee1aea05-2f78-4763-a193-32aabd756b50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**PS:** Pissed off about GOP gerrymandering and want to do something about it? A week out, your $25 or $50 won't move the needle in a Senate or congressional race where tens of millions are already being spent. But in a state House race where only around 40,000 people are expected to vote, it sure can.
Down in southern Wake County, Republican state Rep. Erin Pare voted for the 2023 map that carved up my old district. Then she voted for the Trump-backed map in 2025. Now she's in one of the closest state House races in North Carolina against [Democrat Winn Decker](https://substack.com/redirect/c30da212-d385-444c-9727-c40735516593?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Two years ago Erin Pare won 51% to 45%. This year, even the conservative John Locke Foundation rates her district as a pure toss-up. A race this close could come down to just a few hundred votes. This is one of the few places remaning where last-minute money can make a real difference on election night.

Cook's David Wasserman says that Republicans are falling short of the 10 to 12 seats their strategists first expected to gain from 2025 redistricting, and Cook now projects the likeliest outcome is a net GOP gain of around three seats from redistricting alone, with Democrats strongly favored to win the House. As of this week, Cook has Democrats favored in 220 seats, Republicans in 198, and 17 toss-ups. We only need 218 to elect a Speaker - trust me I know. I've voted for Speaker 19 times when I was in the House. Why? It's no secret. Donald Trump is driving all of this. Well, they are. They're voting against the most corrupt administration in American history. They're voting against a guy who promised to bring prices down and instead made life much more expensive for everyone. And they're voting against his war of choice with Iran, a forever war he dragged us into without ever making the case to Congress or the American people. This is what a really bad year looks like for Trump. Most of the seats the Republicans gerrymandered for Trump are still in play. | | ---|---|--- And the new 13th District? It's looking a little less safe right now. The Cook Political Report moved NC-13 from Solid Republican to Likely Republican. That's a big deal in a district drawn to never be competitive. And it's not just here. Cook moved 19 House races toward Democrats in a single day. Want to track it yourself? The Cook Report keeps a free and page. Why this matters to you | | ---|---|--- When a seat is safe, the only election that counts is the primary. 90% of members of Congress are incentivized only to answer to the loudest slice of their own party, not to voters in November. I told the the biggest divide I found in Congress wasn't Democrat versus Republican. It was safe seats versus competitive seats. When you have to earn every voter's support, you think differently. You focus on solving real problems, and you've got every reason to work across the aisle. That's why I still believe the answer is independent redistricting commissions, like the ones in the I introduced in Congress. The last word I'm on the ballot this year for Wake County District Attorney, and I'm running unopposed in the general election. While I'm grateful for every voter who continues to vote for me - I knew that as soon as I voted for myself the election was over. That's its own little lesson in how sorted we've become. Republicans didn't even bother to field a candidate for District Attorney in Wake County. Now gerrymandering makes winning harder. But it doesn't make your vote meaningless. On November 3rd, the voters get the last word. Make sure you're one of them. Find your polling place and registration info at . Wiley PS: Pissed off about GOP gerrymandering and want to do something about it? A week out, your $25 or $50 won't move the needle in a Senate or congressional race where tens of millions are already being spent. But in a state House race where only around 40,000 people are expected to vote, it sure can. Down in southern Wake County, Republican state Rep. Erin Pare voted for the 2023 map that carved up my old district. Then she voted for the Trump-backed map in 2025. Now she's in one of the closest state House races in North Carolina against . Two years ago Erin Pare won 51% to 45%. This year, even the conservative John Locke Foundation rates her district as a pure toss-up. A race this close could come down to just a few hundred votes. This is one of the few places remaning where last-minute money can make a real difference on election night. ? PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY WILEY FOR WAKE ? Democracy is on the ballot. Join the fight at . | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Wiley for Wake P.O. Box 563, Raleigh, NC 27602 ? ?

The energy and momentum continue to grow, and with just **8 days until Election Day** , we're entering the most important stretch of this campaign! There is still plenty of work to do, and we need your help to finish strong. Whether you can volunteer for a few hours, help us reach voters, or greet voters at the polls on Election Day, **every conversation and every volunteer makes a difference.** Here are some ways you can get involved during the final days of the campaign:

**Thursday, October 29 | 6:30 -7:30 PM | Virtual (Zoom)** Planning to help greet voters at the polls on Election Day? If you've already signed up to poll greet, we strongly encourage you to attend. Everyone is welcome! Peter, in
case you missed it, Trump was here yesterday.

He got up on stage and followed the same MAGA playbook as usual: spew
hatred and try to make people afraid — all so that nobody looks too
closely at gas prices, the never-ending wars, etc.

Small men try to make everyone else feel small. So let’s answer Trump by
going big.

Here’s the plan: we make today one of our best fundraising days of the
entire campaign by setting a goal of reaching 24,000 donations in 24
hours.

I know for a fact that would get under Trump’s skin. It would also knock
the socks off my finance team!

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261026-1-ak.s7cEV2&amount=10&refcode=em20261026-3743&t=1004&akid=3743%2E251025%2E6iR8Xr ]If you’re all-in, pitch in now to help get us started. The size of your
gift doesn't matter. What matters is all of us banding together to take on
Trump and Mike Rogers' billionaire backers:

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261026-1-ak.s7cEV2&amount=10&refcode=em20261026-3743&t=1023&akid=3743%2E251025%2E6iR8Xr ]Donate $10 ››

MAGA money is breaking spending records in Michigan, with $100 million and
counting aimed at our movement. They’ve reserved over $1 million in ad
spending every single day until November 3rd.

And almost every poll we've seen has us statistically tied with Rogers.

I have never taken a dime from corporate PACs, and I never will.

So truly, winning this race all comes down to whether you,
Peter,
and other members of this team can once again beat the big money and send
a people-powered campaign to the U.S. Senate to fight for us, not the
billionaires.

Grassroots money is our only way to fight back, and every one of these
24,000 donations we receive today goes toward making sure Michiganders
hear from us before casting their vote.

Plus, Trump, Rogers, and their MAGA mega donors will find out that each
time he comes to Michigan to spread hate, this movement gets bigger and

I know we’ve been telling you a lot about what happens if we lose

Derek, I know we’ve been telling you a lot about what happens if we lose this must-hold Governor’s seat. clean_body: Our democracy is threatened whenever we take it for granted. | | | | | Peter, In a lot of ways, the people who represent us at the state level have more of an impact on our lives than our elected officials in Washington. That’s why the path to protecting civil rights, fair representation, and elections that reflect the will of the voters runs through America’s statehouses. My friends at the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee lead the national strategy for more than 3,000 state legislators and thousands of Democratic candidates across all 50 states. During my time in the Illinois Senate, I saw how state legislators could use their power to improve the lives of millions of Americans and strengthen our communities. Today’s state legislatures can do the same thing. In fact, with the weakening of democratic norms we’re seeing right now, our state legislatures have never been more important to safeguarding our future. At a moment when our country feels divided and our democracy seems broken, I still believe change only happens when ordinary people get involved and stay engaged. Democrats only have eight days to take advantage of a generational opportunity to win power in the states, and the DLCC is facing critical program gaps that will leave legislative seats vulnerable. | If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process immediately. | | | | | | This work depends on people like you, Peter, who will roll up their sleeves and get to work. Troy Jackson here -- a while back I told you that most fundraising deadlines are bogus. I meant it. Nobody's "urgent quadruple match" ever flipped the Senate blue.

But I am going to explain why our end-of-month fundraising deadline matters so much in the fight to defeat Susan Collins and flip the Senate. **[If you're already with me, chip in now to help us hit our $2,000,000 end-of-month goal before midnight on October 31st. ->](https://substack.com/redirect/b2d4cdfc-4224-47b8-b206-2513689a60be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CHIP IN NOW ->](https://substack.com/redirect/b2d4cdfc-4224-47b8-b206-2513689a60be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
On October 31st, we will sit down and set the budget for the final few days of the campaign based on how much we raised since the beginning of the month.

**How much we raise before then will decide:**

📺 How many TV ads we can book in the final stretch to reach the 4% of undecided voters who will decide this election.

🚪How many organizers we can pay to knock on doors and talk to voters to ensure we can grow our narrow 2-point lead in the polls!

💵 **Whether or not we stand a chance against Susan Collins** and her $114 MILLION in MAGA and billionaire support, because if we lose, Democrats will fail to flip the Senate.
_**That 's it. No sky falling. Just math:**_ what's in the bank account at 11:59 PM decides what we can afford through Election Day, the final days that will decide this election.
**[So if you were ever going to chip in, today is the day to do so. Our $2,000,000 end-of-month fundraising goal is critically important. Can you give whatever you can before October 31st so we can defeat Susan Collins once and for all?->](https://substack.com/redirect/b2d4cdfc-4224-47b8-b206-2513689a60be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CHIP IN NOW ->](https://substack.com/redirect/b2d4cdfc-4224-47b8-b206-2513689a60be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I won't pretend the world ends if you can't. But every dollar you send is a dollar of TV time we don't have to cede to them.

Solidarity forever,
Troy

In July 2021, my husband responded to a call about a suspicious
vehicle at a local truck stop. The driver was disoriented, sweating,
unsteady, and acting erratically. Officers had to use a Taser to take
him into custody.

My husband had a limited role in the arrest - he helped move the
suspect to the patrol car and transported him a short distance to the
police station.

Shortly after arriving at the station, the suspect became unresponsive
and was pronounced dead. After investigating, the state medical
examiner definitively ruled the cause of death as methamphetamine
toxicity.

So imagine our shock when over two years later, the Biden Department
of Justice accused Eddie of "failing to intervene" and a "deliberate
indifference to medical needs" - and charged him under a federal civil
rights statute carrying up to 20 years in prison.

We poured our life savings into Eddie's defense, expecting justice
would prevail at trial and he'd soon be back on the job. But instead,
the government blocked all evidence of the suspect's meth overdose
from the trial.

THE JURY FOUND EDDIE GUILTY - AND HE FACES UP TO 20 YEARS IN PRISON.

Now Eddie will miss graduations and birthdays.

He won't get to walk our daughters down the aisle.

And he'll miss the birth of future grandchildren.

With nowhere to turn, I turned to God and prayed like I've never
prayed before...

And God answered our prayers - in the form of a phone call from Jason
Johnson with the Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF).

For the first time in months, I see a future with Eddie by my side
enjoying our golden years.

But LELDF doesn't receive taxpayer funding or grants, and large gifts
are few and far between.

Instead, LELDF relies on kind-hearted strangers who respect our men
and women in blue and want to help cops like Eddie who are unjustly
convicted.

Folks, I pray, like you.

WILL YOU HELP LELDF FIGHT FOR EDDIE BY MAKING A TAX-DEDUCTIBLE
DONATION OF $35, $50, $100, OR MORE TODAY?
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

No matter how much you're able to help, your donation will be put to
immediate use, helping LELDF support Eddie and a dozen other wrongly
accused officers.

That's why I'm asking you to help LELDF fund Eddie's appeal by making
an urgent donation today.

The appeal will cost approximately $175,000 - SO WHETHER YOU CAN GIVE
$35, $50, $100, $250, $500 OR MORE - EVERY GIFT WILL MAKE A HUGE
DIFFERENCE.

But no matter how much you're able to send in support of Eddie, please
pray for us.

I know firsthand the power of prayer. And I know with LELDF behind us
and an army of prayer warriors beside us, Eddie will win his appeal
and we can move on with our lives.

From the very bottom of my heart, thank you.

With God's blessings,

Jennifer Embly

_Election day is next week! This is how I 'll be voting in Missouri's elections. If helpful, **share this with other voters before election day!**_
The 2026 midterm elections are just eight days away.1
Without a high-profile statewide candidate election, the ballot measures are the marquee issues. The phrasing of ballot measures is often confusing--unfortunately, that's by design--and with so much information and misinformation out there, I wanted to share how I'm voting and why.
Here's how I'll be voting in next week's ballot measures:
* Amendment 3: **Vote NO**
* Amendment 6: **Vote YES**
* Amendment 7: **Vote NO**
* Amendment 8: **Vote NO**
* Proposition A: **Vote NO**

### Amendment 3
The primary goal of Amendment 3 is to reinstate Missouri's ban on abortion access. I've written about [abortion access in the military before](https://substack.com/redirect/cf762099-b003-404a-afa0-b99da301f704?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but I'm also under no misapprehension that I'm going to change anyone's mind on such a thorny and personal topic.
The thing I'll focus on instead is the [ballot candy](https://substack.com/redirect/bd038a12-bf4e-4157-84a6-2a654814bb67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Amendment 3.3 The primary goal may be to ban abortion in the state, but the last bullet point has nothing to do with abortion. Instead, it's about banning gender reassignment surgeries for minors.
What do they neglect to mention? **Gender reassignment surgeries for minors are[already illegal in Missouri](https://substack.com/redirect/151d28d4-dd3d-40fa-81af-8b3acc77c758?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.4
So what's the impact of this ballot measure? It would change nothing about the access minors have to gender reassignment surgery. But **Amendment 3 would reinstate a near-total ban on abortion in the state**.
The yes-on-3 campaign knows it can't win on its own merits, which is why their [most common sign](https://substack.com/redirect/ce53af51-0a3f-4b9a-9ac8-1e6efda5cc24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) says, "ban trans surgeries for minors."5
* [59% of Missourians](https://substack.com/redirect/833b9270-3ef2-472b-8e3c-3f92312917dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) think abortion should be legal within the first eight weeks of pregnancy,6 which is the phase of gestation when the [majority of abortions are happening](https://substack.com/redirect/63773582-09f1-47f1-84dd-8e7d4803549c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).7
* So instead they focus on a more popular issue, banning trans surgeries for minors, a ban that [72% of Missourians support](https://substack.com/redirect/f9c2abd1-bdaf-4fd1-9d4f-7adf4855c3e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).8

Missouri Republicans have [openly admitted to including policies related to gender reassignment surgery](https://substack.com/redirect/97e0e71b-8497-4113-bf10-1e953d5f4628?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) because it'll help Amendment 3 pass, despite the fact that it would change nothing about its legality in Missouri.
When they admit that they're trying to trick us, we probably should listen to them.
**I 'm voting NO on Amendment 3.**

When I write about Missouri, a [pretty](https://substack.com/redirect/bd038a12-bf4e-4157-84a6-2a654814bb67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [consistent](https://substack.com/redirect/cf9f89e3-4660-47dd-80b7-ee33cd9c9f67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [theme](https://substack.com/redirect/8fb4ce50-b278-4775-948e-6d709c8e674a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is that the state legislature regularly tries to mess around with the ballot measure process:

We've seen two things happening time and again:
* The legislature [rolling](https://substack.com/redirect/9ddcd37f-3f1a-47f4-8904-6d7b3f8291d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [back](https://substack.com/redirect/f41bfd64-bbbf-43ac-9b4b-6100c767d8dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [laws](https://substack.com/redirect/0a86988f-efd3-4b65-98b7-b6a3aa7dbe14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [that](https://substack.com/redirect/6414a55b-7459-4f3d-987c-f9057cd11738?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [Missourians](https://substack.com/redirect/469660a2-51c6-4125-b1ca-4b826f656e3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [pass](https://substack.com/redirect/017c9492-78c4-4e34-9271-e5d24a7cbeee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) via ballot measure.
* Missouri's Secretary of State [consistently](https://substack.com/redirect/3042d846-386d-4f93-8753-8783bc857863?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [writes](https://substack.com/redirect/85ef70d6-7a32-434d-b122-aec63077f12d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [misleading](https://substack.com/redirect/eb2ab10a-0484-4262-b377-505101dbe5e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [ballot](https://substack.com/redirect/3175e7e0-bcb3-41ca-9a7d-ac8c71ee4915?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [language](https://substack.com/redirect/21b35481-8a92-48d6-8442-592ad69b66d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), with the express goal of misleading voters. (This isn't my opinion; Secretary of State Denny Hoskins has [literally admitted to doing this in court](https://substack.com/redirect/3175e7e0-bcb3-41ca-9a7d-ac8c71ee4915?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).)

The status quo isn't working, and elected officials are getting [more creative in trying to mess around](https://substack.com/redirect/cf9f89e3-4660-47dd-80b7-ee33cd9c9f67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with the ballot measure process. **Amendment 6 would meaningfully protect the ballot measure process** :
1. It requires fair, neutral, and easy-to-understand ballot language.
2. It makes it significantly harder for the legislature to throw out legislation that Missourians pass at the ballot box.
3. It enshrines the right to initiate and pass ballot measures in the state constitution.

Future reforms depend on Amendment 6 passing.
**I 'm voting YES on Amendment 6.**
### Amendment 7
This would basically create a [sovereign wealth fund](https://substack.com/redirect/e2e15e04-2356-41b4-9c13-7e83e2beead7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for Missouri, with the goal of using it [in about a century](https://substack.com/redirect/8bdec57e-9b9e-4ba4-9f97-760f600191f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to get rid of all state taxes.
I have no problem with the concept of a sovereign wealth fund, and I think sovereign wealth funds in [Alaska](https://substack.com/redirect/475ef075-6c2a-45ca-8ab7-011149e8ab6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/123a2b9e-d9e9-4afd-a0ed-38e1892488ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)9 actually work pretty well. The problem is that the way that this amendment is structured is totally half-baked.10
The majority of sovereign wealth funds are [funded by revenues from natural resources](https://substack.com/redirect/958bcc6d-5d41-49cd-ab35-da8e317f29fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) like oil and gas. That's how it works in Alaska, Texas, and [every other U.S. state with a sovereign wealth fund](https://substack.com/redirect/6044f1fc-ae26-486d-9894-2286a68f53d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
But [it's totally unclear](https://substack.com/redirect/8bdec57e-9b9e-4ba4-9f97-760f600191f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) how the so-called "Show-Me Prosperity Fund" would be funded. There's just this abstract idea that some hypothetical surplus money could go into a sovereign wealth fund, at the same time that the state is already staring down some [pretty substantial budget cuts](https://substack.com/redirect/794d6822-575b-47f2-a51a-31937f43ac20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
I'm struggling to find a single example of anyone trying something like this anywhere in the world.11 The idea that Missouri can somehow squirrel away money now to avoid taxes in a century is completely unserious.
**I 'm voting NO on Amendment 7.**

### Amendment 8
This would weaken counties' power to remove sheriffs, instead [consolidating that power with the attorney general](https://substack.com/redirect/b8d01e56-6522-4435-8c49-51607708ba30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Given the last few attorneys general we've had and the ways they've been behaving, I'm not inclined to imbue that role with more power.
It would also require counties to elect their sheriffs, though most counties in the state [already do that](https://substack.com/redirect/aa2e410c-0de7-42d5-8eee-6c5e86790f00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
I'll be honest--this is the least consequential statewide ballot measure in this election. But it's still bad policy.
**I 'm voting NO on Amendment 8.**

### What about all the judges?
On my ballot, I'm being asked whether to retain 19 judges. These are bizarre elections: [they very rarely result in any judge](https://substack.com/redirect/ab0277ae-e2b4-49d7-9f75-d8a24c61de6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) losing their position.12
This is a testament to the strength of the [Missouri Plan](https://substack.com/redirect/56c88791-9560-4ab1-b60c-8ffdcd44784a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a nonpartisan means of selecting judges for appointment that's been used in the state for 85 years and adopted (in whole or in part) by dozens of other states.
These elections are important; they're also lower turnout, because people get tired of filling in the bubbles.13
The Missouri Bar [recommends retaining every judge](https://substack.com/redirect/4221b693-19af-45d2-aad9-4af8b3e179db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I won't opine on each of these, but I will opine on one: Supreme Court judge [Paul Wilson](https://substack.com/redirect/ee360593-a430-4b03-90cb-b21e2d2cb644?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I don't agree with him on everything, but over the past year, he's consistently sided with voters and with democracy.
Despite immense pressure from statewide elected officials and from the federal government, he and a majority of the court stood up for fair ballot language, for fair courts, and for the state constitution.
**I 'm voting YES to retain Paul Wilson on the Supreme Court**.

* 78.6% of abortions happen before 10 weeks.
* 92.8% of abortions happen before 14 weeks.

1.1% of abortions happen after 20 weeks, often because of fetal abnormalities or other issues, though I couldn't find reliable data to quantify that exactly.
For context, [from the polling above](https://substack.com/redirect/833b9270-3ef2-472b-8e3c-3f92312917dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg): 47% of Missourians say that abortion should be legal through the first 12 weeks of pregnancy; 43% say it shouldn't be.
8
This is basically in line with the rest of America: [74% support a ban on gender reassignment surgeries](https://substack.com/redirect/4420e3e8-a67d-4dca-aad6-63ce2b47058d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for those under 18.
9
Or [Saudi Arabia](https://substack.com/redirect/e6b8d67d-2960-4b7c-b2d9-ad8b01b3e13b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), or [Norway](https://substack.com/redirect/c070550b-ea54-473a-8680-dd6e05df8ecf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), or [Qatar](https://substack.com/redirect/ad827bb3-d301-4094-829c-078b6b12f304?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
10
It's the same sort of issue with Amendment 5 back in August, which [lost spectacularly](https://substack.com/redirect/633bd9b6-5cf8-4aa3-a8de-32cf6c1ab51d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
[](https://substack.com/redirect/7702d38e-cb1e-4a8d-a8c1-9218590cea9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |

I had no philosophical issue getting rid of the state's income tax, but they gave no thought to what would replace it. Amendment 7 was crafted with similar thoughtlessness.
11
In 2014, West Virginia set up a sovereign wealth fund meant to be backed by the state's coal and oil resources. But without any initial funding, no money ever went in, and it was [eventually abolished](https://substack.com/redirect/eae5e019-6f23-4fd5-8f7c-567e91ce42f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) less than a decade later.
What Missouri is trying is basically the failed West Virginia plan without having even the theoretical natural resource revenue to commit.
12
Since the so-called Missouri Plan was implemented in 1940, [only four judges](https://substack.com/redirect/ab0277ae-e2b4-49d7-9f75-d8a24c61de6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) have been ousted in a retention vote.
13
In the last election, [about 14% of the people](https://substack.com/redirect/35b6e88c-fd4a-4ab7-a868-9534d94b5593?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who voted for president didn't participate in the state Supreme Court retention elections.

If helpful, share this with other voters before election day! The 2026 midterm elections are just eight days away.1 Without a high-profile statewide candidate election, the ballot measures are the marquee issues. The phrasing of ballot measures is often confusing--unfortunately, that's by design--and with so much information and misinformation out there, I wanted to share how I'm voting and why. Here's how I'll be voting in next week's ballot measures: Amendment 3: Vote NO Amendment 6: Vote YES Amendment 7: Vote NO Amendment 8: Vote NO Proposition A: Vote NO I will also be voting YES to retain Judge Paul Wilson. More on why those are my votes, and more on the other votes you'll have, throughout this article.2 Amendment 3 The primary goal of Amendment 3 is to reinstate Missouri's ban on abortion access. I've written about , but I'm also under no misapprehension that I'm going to change anyone's mind on such a thorny and personal topic. The thing I'll focus on instead is the in Amendment 3.3 The primary goal may be to ban abortion in the state, but the last bullet point has nothing to do with abortion. Instead, it's about banning gender reassignment surgeries for minors. What do they neglect to mention? Gender reassignment surgeries for minors are So what's the impact of this ballot measure? It would change nothing about the access minors have to gender reassignment surgery. But Amendment 3 would reinstate a near-total ban on abortion in the state. The yes-on-3 campaign knows it can't win on its own merits, which is why their says, "ban trans surgeries for minors."5 think abortion should be legal within the first eight weeks of pregnancy,6 which is the phase of gestation when the So instead they focus on a more popular issue, banning trans surgeries for minors, a ban that Missouri Republicans have because it'll help Amendment 3 pass, despite the fact that it would change nothing about its legality in Missouri. When they admit that they're trying to trick us, we probably should listen to them. I 'm voting NO on Amendment 3. The status quo isn't working, and elected officials are getting with the ballot measure process. Amendment 6 would meaningfully protect the ballot measure process : 1. It requires fair, neutral, and easy-to-understand ballot language. 2. It makes it significantly harder for the legislature to throw out legislation that Missourians pass at the ballot box. 3. It enshrines the right to initiate and pass ballot measures in the state constitution. Future reforms depend on Amendment 6 passing. I 'm voting YES on Amendment 6. Amendment 7 This would basically create a for Missouri, with the goal of using it to get rid of all state taxes. I have no problem with the concept of a sovereign wealth fund, and I think sovereign wealth funds in and actually work pretty well. The problem is that the way that this amendment is structured is totally half-baked.10 The majority of sovereign wealth funds are like oil and gas. That's how it works in Alaska, Texas, and . But how the so-called "Show-Me Prosperity Fund" would be funded. There's just this abstract idea that some hypothetical surplus money could go into a sovereign wealth fund, at the same time that the state is already staring down some . I'm struggling to find a single example of anyone trying something like this anywhere in the world.11 The idea that Missouri can somehow squirrel away money now to avoid taxes in a century is completely unserious. I 'm voting NO on Amendment 7. Amendment 8 This would weaken counties' power to remove sheriffs, instead . Given the last few attorneys general we've had and the ways they've been behaving, I'm not inclined to imbue that role with more power. It would also require counties to elect their sheriffs, though most counties in the state . I'll be honest--this is the least consequential statewide ballot measure in this election. But it's still bad policy. I 'm voting NO on Amendment 8. Proposition A I already , so I won't belabor the point. Voting NO strikes down Missouri's gerrymandered congressional maps. It's a no-brainer. I 'm voting NO on Proposition A. What about all the judges? On my ballot, I'm being asked whether to retain 19 judges. These are bizarre elections: losing their position.12 This is a testament to the strength of the , a nonpartisan means of selecting judges for appointment that's been used in the state for 85 years and adopted (in whole or in part) by dozens of other states. These elections are important; they're also lower turnout, because people get tired of filling in the bubbles.13 The Missouri Bar . I won't opine on each of these, but I will opine on one: Supreme Court judge . I don't agree with him on everything, but over the past year, he's consistently sided with voters and with democracy. Despite immense pressure from statewide elected officials and from the federal government, he and a majority of the court stood up for fair ballot language, for fair courts, and for the state constitution. I 'm voting YES to retain Paul Wilson on the Supreme Court. What about the local ballot measures? There are too many to opine on--about 100 local and county ballot measures, by my count. subject: It’s all about turnout now
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ANDY FOR NEVADA
body:
Where things stand in this race... | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/andyfornevada/friday-weekly-5860062?e=6736d7bc47)
---
| | [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/7fvUd3K2XdH?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)
---
| | Dear Peter,

With only eight days to go before Election Day, the data that’s been pouring in regarding early and mail voting is pointing to a few things:

1. It appears that there is no Blue Wave materializing in Nevada, by which I mean that Democrat turnout does not seem to be at a level that puts victory out of reach for Republicans.

2. Republicans, nonetheless, are running behind where we need to be in order to win this year — though, given that Republicans are historically more likely to vote on Election Day itself, this is something we can still overcome.

3. Therefore, it is now all about turnout.

We are well positioned to win this election — _if_ Republicans show up to vote, either during this final week of early voting, or on Election Day.

So I’ve got another list of three for you. There are three things I’m asking you to do:

1. Make sure you vote. If you’ve already voted, great — and thank you! If you haven’t yet voted, make a plan to. If you want to vote early and don’t know where to do so, please go [here](https://us.list-manage.com/oBdz1xtBsZc?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) to find out.

2. Encourage your friends, family members and neighbors to vote. Make sure they know the stakes, and make it clear to them that this election is shaping up to be very close, meaning _every single vote counts_.

3. If you can, please [make a contribution](https://us.list-manage.com/G9SHUsGLo1a?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) to my campaign. Every dollar we raise from here on out is going directly into our get-out-the-vote efforts. A contribution of $100 allows us to reach more than 1,500 voters here in the home stretch. We’ll be encouraging Republican voters to turn out and vote for me, but this will of course help our candidates up and down the ballot as well. [You can contribute today by clicking here.](https://us.list-manage.com/EMzC2k0AskY?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)

As always, thank you, my friend, for all your support and for your commitment to our shared principles. As I said, we’re in a position to win this race — and I hope you’ll help us get across the finish line.

Until next time...

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

Today, early voting is underway in both states, and the initial numbers

turnout. But Texas’s GOP stronghold of Denton County also smashed its own
record, a sign of enthusiasm on both sides.

subject: Faith paired with action
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Troy Downing for Congress
body:
When I put God first, everything else falls into place

| Peter,**
**People ask me how I keep going when the attacks pile up, the polls tighten, and the Democrats have their sights on stealing our House majority.
[ The honest answer is God, family, and country.](https://trk.emails.troydowning.-hTTyl_XiqA)
---
| [SEND A PRAYER](https://trk.emails.troydowning.-k42Xw)
---
When I put God first, everything else falls into place – including the strength to keep fighting for our conservative way of life even when the odds and the opposition say I shouldn't.**
**This midterm cycle will test that resolve more than any election I've been part of. The other side knows exactly how much is riding on these next few weeks, and they're spending like it.**
**I believe faith is what keeps our mission going when times get hard – but faith paired with action is what actually wins elections.**
**But I'm not writing to sell you anything or tell you something I’m sure you already know. **
**I'm writing to ask for something simple: say a prayer for our majority tonight, and for every candidate across this country fighting to keep this House intact.
[And if your faith moves you to back it up with a gift, every dollar – even $5 – helps us keep sharing that message with voters who haven't made up their minds yet.](https://trk.emails.troydowning.-Q)
---
| [SEND A PRAYER](https://trk.emails.troydowning.)
---
God Bless you, Peter,
Troy Downing (MT-02)

Early voting ends Friday! Plus, an update from the campaign trail and an invitation to Election Night.
| | | | Last Week To Vote Early
This is the final week of early voting! Early voting ends this Friday, October 30, and Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. If you haven't voted yet, make a plan to cast your ballot this week.
You can find your early voting location and hours by clicking below.
---
| [](https://a89bm49ab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0011p2UUHLXS33qAp-BOa7ULZxAuE68qKp7zr_f-oUt7OMYXHjKTeoKFnCrNeFTlghq0poXod602A7Tpevijb2IUgXN-TKKHQycA_gKMh16NEW1gcd_aNY7qCQpOx9hsf7DRMXiiEvTAKeUEncdXdXZIm_RI3G9Az67Bkhg8RtHW1TCicTXWrhvqNh0sCHPmiXbEH69v4siU7U=&c=V-qvN0ZXG5cbOisPJT06idysONl8aLWXMBFCtZQjHQamsxesuSZkLA==&ch=YmtLU5Nj3PFC9ngivxeICZAcftCxGcxJKocsugv8N4eTCgkXiITRzw==)
---

| A MASSIVE Thank You!
---
| When I launched this campaign last summer, I knew it would take a lot of hard work, but I also knew we had an incredible team of friends and supporters behind us. Over the past 15 months, that support has meant more to me than I can put into words.
As we enter the final days of this campaign, I simply want to say THANK YOU. Whether you've volunteered, contributed, put up a sign, attended an event, or kept us in your prayers, you've helped make this campaign possible. Gabi and I are incredibly grateful for each and every person who has helped us through this journey.
We're almost at the finish line, and I couldn't be more excited about the opportunity to represent the 10th District in Congress. Let's finish strong and celebrate a big victory on November 3!
---
| |
---
| |
---
| On the Trail
---
| It's been another busy week on the campaign trail! In the last week alone, we've visited more than half of the 10th District's 20 counties, and we're not slowing down!
We've had great campaign meet & greets in Franklin, Greene, Putnam, and Jasper counties, and we've enjoyed campaigning alongside our fellow Republican candidates up and down the ballot in several other counties. From celebrating a $1 million investment in Elbert County Memorial Hospital to honoring veterans in Barrow County and visiting with friends and supporters across the district, we've covered a lot of ground!
The best part of traveling across the district has been hearing directly from the people we hope to represent in Congress. Every stop has reinforced why we're running and how much is at stake in this election.
We're giving this final stretch everything we've got. 8 days until victory!
---

Sign Waving on Election Day: If you can wave signs on Election Day, please email James so we can get you a sign and high-traffic location.
To sign up for ANY of these volunteer opportunities, please email James at [James@houstongaines.com](mailto:james@houstongaines.com)

body:
8 days left

| Peter, there are a few good lessons trick-or-treating teaches you:

• Always say please and thank you.
• Be a good neighbor.
• Never eat too many M&M’s in one sitting (a lesson I’m still learning).
• And remember that every door matters. When one house hands out Tootsie Rolls, you keep going. The next one might have full-size candy bars!

I still remember the excitement of dressing up as a little girl and going door to door for candy. In a different season of life, I fondly remember taking my daughter trick-or-treating in our neighborhood.

Those days may be behind me, but I got a little bit of that magic back this year. I've been knocking on doors all across Iowa, and what a joy it's been! Behind every door is an Iowan with a story and a voice that deserves to be heard in Congress. I've met so many wonderful Iowans at their doorsteps. People who've welcomed me into conversations about their families, their farms, their small businesses, their worries, and their hopes for the future. People who may not agree on everything (even some who've voted for my opponent in the past!), but who all deserve to know that someone in Congress is listening to them.

I can't wait to get to Congress and make sure those voices are heard. But first, we have an election to win. We're in the final stretch, and we're working hard to reach every voter we can before Election Day. Will you help us keep going by making a donation to our $75,000 end-of-month goal? >> **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cb-q4-2026?refcode2=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142205514/656153244/-2014245750?refcode=em26_261026_eom2_fnd_clq_act___cp_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_261026_eom2_fnd_clq_act___cp_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=ecfea18b-45d1-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjIyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlY2ZlYTE4Yi00NWQxLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dFOQxWp1mPJ6-wcDPEpaYkcFFqOiR5IcHgE34LSM5rY=)**

subject: My decision

body:
Here's the truth
Peter –
As I was having my coffee yesterday morning, I was thinking about my journey to this moment. I never imagined that I would be here today, representing the people of Virginia’s 7th district, and fighting for our future in Congress.
I’m a Jewish-Ukrainian immigrant whose family came to America to find hope like so many others, and I was proud to join the military and serve my country.
When my brother, Lt. Col. Alexander Vindman, heard President Trump’s infamous call with Ukraine, we knew our oath to defend our country and the Constitution required us to report the call up the chain of command.
Because we did not let Trump's abuse of his office stand, he was impeached — and his vengeance cost us our careers when we were fired in retaliation.
Back then, I never thought I would run for Congress. But in the years following, we saw Republicans go all-in on authoritarianism. And to this day, with Donald Trump in office, that threat exists. More than ever.
It started with the attempted coup of January 6th, Trump and his allies illegally meddling in fair elections, and the GOP rolling back our fundamental rights.
Now, it's the attacks against working people. The corruption. The stripping of healthcare away from millions of families. And another endless war in the Middle East risking the lives of our service members and raising costs here at home.
Throughout it all, I've stood my ground. I’ve fought for working families and been a voice for our service members. And I’ve even dared to hold Trump accountable again on the House floor, knowing I would face his vengeance once again. And to no one’s surprise, I did. He launched a sham investigation into me to kick me out of Congress.
But not for a second did I doubt my decisions, Peter. Why? Because we can’t sit by while our country is brought to its breaking point like this.
So when I heard the call to serve two years ago, I did what I always did. I answered it.
But the reality is that threat remains — and its not going anywhere as long as Trump’s minions in Congress continue to grant him unchecked power.
So now I am trying to continue my service in Congress. For you. For our democracy. And for the future of our republic.
But I cannot do this alone. I need your help to get across the finish line. The path to the House majority and putting a check on Trump’s power runs through VA-07, and we cannot fall behind on our fundraising if we want to have the resources we need to win this race.

body:
We’re collecting food, water, new clothing, and more for families hit by the flooding.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/Dm1SWWuNR2v?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810)
| |
# Three days to help flood victims. Here’s where to drop off.
---
|
---
| | | | | | Friend,
I have had the opportunity to tour any of the devastated areas of New Mexico and have seen and heard first-hand what their needs are. Families across New Mexico are dealing with the aftermath of the flooding. Some have lost their belongings. Some have lost their homes. All of them could use a hand from their neighbors right now.
That’s why the Hull for New Mexico campaign and the Republican Party of New Mexico are hosting a Flood Donation Drive this week, and I’m asking you to be part of it.
**When:** Monday, October 26 through Wednesday, October 28, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. each day
**Where to drop off:**
RPNM Headquarters, 5150 San Francisco Rd NE, Ste A, Albuquerque, NM 87109
Gregg Hull Campaign Office, 2201 San Pedro Dr NE, Bldg 1, Ste 200, Albuquerque, NM 87110
**What’s needed:**
Canned food, bottled water, new clothing, new blankets, toiletries, and new toys for the kids
[**FOR MONETARY DONATIONS, VISIT REDCROSS.ORG**](https://us.list-manage.com/FpME52DTTZ_?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810).
You don’t have to bring a lot. A case of water or a bag of canned goods makes a real difference to a family starting over. If you can’t make it yourself, forward this to a friend, a coworker, or your church group who can.
This isn’t about politics. It’s about New Mexicans showing up for each other, the way we always have.
I hope to see you this week.
---
| | | | |
---
| |
**P.S.** Not sure what to bring? Water and canned food go the fastest. Drop off anytime between 10 AM and 4 PM, Monday through Wednesday.

Team, Did you see this? Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth just announced that our military’s cyber forces – the U.S. Cyber Command – will work with the Department of Homeland Security to defend our elections from any foreign interference. But Trump has gutted critical election security infrastructure since he entered the White House – including the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) that was designed to ensure our elections are free, fair, and safe. _As one expert put it:_ | | | _**“If the administration was serious about assisting state and local election officials, they shouldn’t have dismantled all of the federal government’s election cybersecurity capacity and fired all their experts in early 2025.”** \- Former DOJ Attorney David Becker_
---|---|---
This is the same administration that has pushed countless conspiracy theories about our election system – that Trump won the 2020 election, that our elections are "rigged" against him and MAGA Republicans, and that there's widespread voter fraud.
So with the midterms approaching, voters have every right to ask what this announcement is really about – and whether putting a close Trump ally like Pete Hegseth in charge of "watching" our elections will protect them or put them at risk.
**Democratic Secretaries of State are the ones standing between voters and these attacks. Their job is to make sure every eligible person can vote, and make sure every vote counts.**

body:
My team has to look beyond the election because when that ruling comes, whichever way it goes, we need to be ready to turn on a dime and respond.
#

Hey friend, it’s Mark.
I know you’re probably wondering why, with about a week until the election, I’m writing to ask you to make a donation. And I know that the least I can do is offer you an explanation. I owe you that.
So, if you can, give me 60 seconds to get you up to speed on exactly where things stand.
Last year, I repeated something every single servicemember is taught. For that, the President of the United States said I should be arrested, tried for sedition, and hanged. His Secretary of Defense threatened me with court-martial, censured me, and moved to reduce the rank and pension I earned over 25 years in uniform.
In January, I sued the Secretary of Defense. I never imagined I'd have to do something like that in my life. A federal judge heard the case and ruled in my favor — he rejected Hegseth's arguments. Almost before the ink was dry, Hegseth appealed.
Since that appeal, we’ve been waiting. My team has to look beyond the election because when that ruling comes, whichever way it goes, we need to be ready to turn on a dime and respond.
Here's what I keep coming back to. Hegseth didn't have to appeal. He’s coming after me because Trump’s ordering him to. He's doing it in public, so every other servicemember and veteran in this country can see it.
That's the whole point. It was never just about me. It's about making sure the next person thinks twice before they speak out.
I'm not going to let that happen. But I can't do it on my own.

Maine's investigation into how 498 blank absentee ballot return envelopes ended up in Maryland was closed without an answer after UPS said it would need a subpoena to share its records and the Attorney General's office determined there was not enough information to issue one, according to state investigative reports.
"The AG's Office determined there was not enough information to issue a subpoena for this case," Secretary of State Detective Ray Goodspeed wrote in records obtained under the Freedom of Access Act.
The investigation stemmed from a series of election blunders in Oct. 2025. As first exposed by _[The Robinson Report](http://Only in response to) , _a woman in Newburgh found 250 absentee ballots in an Amazon package delivered to her house. Then a political non-profit in the DC area disclosed that it has received a box of Maine absentee ballot affidavit envelopes.

Secretary of State Shenna Bellows initially promised to investigate both election security breaches until a "bad actor" responsible for the mishandled voting materials was identified. However, Bellows has never announced the conclusion of either investigation.

#### [Maine Woman Finds Bundles of Election Ballots in Amazon Package](https://substack.com/redirect/bea245df-0ce7-4e04-8c33-d0f2231e7417?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| [| Read full story

The closest Bellows came to answering lingering questions over the ballot security issue was to blame UPS. In October 2025, Bellows' office moved Election Day ballot deliveries from UPS to a different courier, Vital Delivery.
"UPS fell down on the job, and that's why the State of Maine does not use them for ballot delivery anymore," Bellows said, speaking about the Newburgh ballots a year later.
According to the documents obtained by _The Robinson Report_ , the investigation into the envelopes ended in the spring -- with no announcement.
In March 2026, investigators wrote that their ability to determine why the envelopes went to Maryland "remains speculative," and the case was closed pending additional information.
On at least two occasions, Bellows refused to disclose the name of the political NGO that had received Maine absentee ballot envelopes. Her office even ignored requests from ranking lawmakers on the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee.
The office disclosed the name of the group that received the envelopes, the Center for Civic Design, to me in a Freedom of Access Act reply on Sept. 28, 2026, 36 days before Election Day. It released the investigative reports and 47 pages of emails on Oct. 23 in response to my FOAA request.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7172d610-f218-47de-b488-32623e28f638?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Secretary of State Detective Ray Goodspeed's report: the 498-envelope count, the UPS subpoena and the "speculative" conclusion.
### The courier switch
On Tuesday, Oct. 14, 2025, the state's elections director notified towns of the change.
"Official (Election Day) ballots are beginning to ship. Please note that your ballots will be delivered by a different courier, Vital Delivery," Heidi Peckham, director of elections and voter registration, wrote in an email reported by The Maine Wire.
Kate McBrien, Bellows' chief deputy and chief of staff, tied future UPS business to the investigation in an October 2025 email to the company.
"Our office remains hopeful that we can work with UPS again for the next election cycle, but that will be dependent on getting answers -- wherever they may lead -- in the current investigation, so we can ensure that it never happens again," McBrien wrote.
In the same reply, she wrote that Bellows "is equally concerned that a package of absentee ballot envelopes was reboxed, relabeled and mailed to a third party with which neither the printer nor the State of Maine has any relationship."
On Dec. 4, 2025, AG's office Detective David Caron "requested tracking details for the packages involved in this case, as well as any video surveillance of this package in UPS's custody," Goodspeed wrote.
On Feb. 6, 2026, "UPS advised that they would need a subpoena to provide additional information from UPS concerning the shipments of envelopes."
The AG's office did not issue one.
Earlier in the report, Goodspeed wrote that it "was later determined that there was no legal basis for the Maine AG's Office to subpoena records from UPS for the absentee voter ballot envelopes that arrived in Maryland."
A UPS spokesperson has previously said the company fully cooperated with the state.
On the Amazon ballots, the spokesperson said, "This was due to an unintentional error on the part of our package handlers."
### The missing box
On Sept. 10, 2025, Adam Graphic Corp. of North Attleboro, Massachusetts, shipped the elections office's order.
The shipment was "sixty-two (62) packages, each containing five hundred (500) envelopes," Secretary of State Detective James E. Gordon wrote. The elections office received 61.
"One box of envelopes and other election day supplies was noted as missing by our office on 9/11," McBrien wrote.
The records do not show the state learning where the box was until the evening of Oct. 3, 2025, when a CCD employee whose name the state redacted emailed the elections bureau.
"I am contacting you to report that we have erroneously received a box of blank return mail envelopes that appear to be for Maine via UPS," the employee wrote.
"Around September 13, 2025, a box arrived at the Center for Civic Design office in Cambridge, Maryland. The box contained approximately 100 blank absentee ballot return envelopes. ... The envelopes remained inside the box at our office during that time and were not accessed by anyone," the employee wrote.
The employee also wrote, "I have placed the box of return envelopes in a secure storage locker so that they cannot be tampered with."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/792f4966-42fd-40e4-af65-f8abee88d5fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Center for Civic Design's Oct. 3, 2025, email to the elections bureau. The sender's name was redacted by the state. (Long lines were re-wrapped as image strips for readability; a few characters at the wrap points are clipped.)
The detectives' count differs.
"The box contained 498 of the 500 absentee voter ballot envelopes that were missing," Goodspeed wrote after the count at the Bureau of Motor Vehicles in Augusta. The records don't explain the gap between "approximately 100" and 498, or what happened to the other two.
The CCD email describes an "office." Goodspeed's report says the CCD contact "recalled that the package was left unattended at her front door."
That confusion is likely explained by the location of CCD's office: a residential property in Maryland.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2b0eb9db-7bd0-4b72-83cd-7ae03dc2edde?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The CCD office in Maryland where Maine absentee ballot envelopes were shipped.
### The tracking
The state's printer told investigators it did not ship anything to CCD.
The Adam Graphic employee "informed me that the Center for Civic Design is not a customer of Adam Graphic Corporation, so they could not have shipped a package to them," Gordon wrote.
Tracking for the missing box "had been checked in transit and at one point indicated that the package was out for delivery," Gordon wrote, but later "the only history was that the label was created."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ba1cc467-1421-4253-8061-d78f6ca04beb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Detective James E. Gordon's report: 62 packages of 500, and Adam Graphic's statement that CCD "is not a customer."
The label on the box shipped it from "UPS OVERGOODS" in Chelmsford, Massachusetts, to the Center for Civic Design.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a30e6752-159a-423a-a4cd-267e4d746f5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The UPS label on the box: shipped from "UPS OVERGOODS" in Chelmsford, Massachusetts, to the Center for Civic Design. Phone number blurred. (The blur also partly covers the first "CENTER FOR CIVIC" line.)
Goodspeed's report says only that it is "believed" this was the same parcel meant for Augusta. The records don't explain how a return-to-sender package came to be addressed to CCD.
Goodspeed concluded: "Without the cooperation of UPS or a violation of Maine Criminal Statutes to justify formal legal requests, further leads or information are unlikely to develop. As a result, our ability to determine why the absentee voter envelopes were redirected from their original destination to Maryland remains speculative. This investigation will be closed pending additional information that will justify re-examination."
On April 2, 2026, the department's enforcement director described the case's status.
"The envelope case is closed, and that did not go to the AG's Office. We can provide that to you, as they did not want to look at it," Derek Dinsmore, director of the Enforcement Services Division, wrote to McBrien.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f587c4d8-6df4-4d27-8b33-e57557288da1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Enforcement Services Director Derek Dinsmore, April 2, 2026: "that did not go to the AG's Office." Crop ends before an unrelated sentence about an AG staffer.
### "We do not work with" CCD
The morning after the CCD email, McBrien wrote to investigators, copying Bellows and Attorney General Aaron Frey.
"We do not work with the Center for Civic Design as a vendor for anything," McBrien wrote.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/28a12c10-1ce8-41b1-91a9-853de49a9cd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Chief Deputy Kate McBrien's Oct. 4, 2025, email, copied to Bellows and Frey: "We do not work with the Center for Civic Design as a vendor for anything." Missing letters are a defect of the PDF the state produced. (Re-wrapped strips.)
Despite the lack of a commercial relationship with CCD, CCD has lobbied the Secretary of State's office on various election related matters.
On Jan. 16, 2025, Emma Werowinski, CCD's design lead, who previously designed ranked-choice voting materials for New York voting groups, invited elections staffer Melissa Packard to join "our Implementing RCV group on the Civic Roundtable platform."
On June 9, 2025, Alysia Melnick, a Bernstein Shur attorney and registered lobbyist who was on the ACLU of Maine's legislative team when Bellows ran it, wrote to Emily Cook, then Bellows' communications director and now a deputy secretary of state. Melnick wrote that "we believe our friends at US Digital Response or Center for Civic Design would be happy to help." Cook forwarded it to Bellows. "The bill already passed the Senate... call when you're free?" Cook wrote.
On July 28, 2026, Jocelyn Bucaro, Denver's former elections director, signing as a CCD communications consultant, emailed Bellows and McBrien directly. CCD Executive Director Sean Wang, who previously held team leadership positions at Arabella Advisors, was copied.
"I'm excited to share a new resource you may be interested in from the Center for Civic Design," Bucaro wrote. "Would you be available for a brief meeting in the next couple weeks?"
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/daf326a7-0a46-4d45-87ee-4ae3d34c6293?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
CCD consultant Jocelyn Bucaro's July 28, 2026, email to Bellows. Phone blurred.
On Aug. 14, 2026, Joann Bautista, Bellows' former deputy secretary of state, who started in the job in 2021 and is now with the Bipartisan Policy Center, emailed the same CCD toolkit to New England election officials, including Maine Deputy Secretary of State Julie Flynn.
"I wanted to share a resource from The Center for Civic Design," Bautista wrote.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cdf48a4f-85f3-40d5-b522-1e291d600691?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Former Deputy Secretary of State Joann Bautista's Aug. 14, 2026, email sharing CCD's toolkit. Phone blurred.
