body:
Trump's MAGA megadonor allies are pouring money into these races, and they're not going to let up in the final eight days.
#
Hey Peter, it's Tim.
In just a moment, **[I'm going to ask if you'll make a contribution to Small Town PAC before our final October 31 end-of-month fundraising deadline.](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261026-2.ppfaXa&amount=5&refcode=em20261026-1261&t=1&akid=1261%2E34582%2E9LZWnV)** Before I do, I hope you'll let me explain why this matters.
Small Town PAC is working to help Democrats compete in places too many people have written off — by backing good people who understand their communities and know what working families are up against.
When I launched this organization back in April, that's exactly what I set out to do. And now, with just eight days until Election Day, we're putting that mission to work.
We've endorsed teachers, working parents, and public servants running for Congress in Minnesota, Iowa, and Pennsylvania. And just last week, we added three more candidates running for governor in Wisconsin, Ohio, and Kansas.
These are people who are showing up, listening to their neighbors, and fighting for communities that Washington too often leaves behind.
**But here's the deal: Trump's MAGA megadonor allies are pouring money into these races, and they're not going to let up in the final eight days.**
Our candidates need to be able to fight back against Republican attacks, get their messages in front of voters, and turn out every last supporter. That takes resources, and it takes getting those resources to them while there's still time to put them to work.
We have just five days to reach our $75,000 end-of-month goal. After Saturday's deadline, there will be only three days left until Election Day. We can't afford to come up short and wish we'd done more when it's too late to make a difference.
_That's why I'm asking for your help now, Peter._
**[Will you chip in $5 or whatever works for you to help Small Town PAC reach our $75,000 goal before October 31 and give our endorsed candidates the support they need to finish strong on November 3?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261026-2.ppfaXa&amount=5&refcode=em20261026-1261&t=2&akid=1261%2E34582%2E9LZWnV)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261026-2.ppfaXa&amount=5&refcode=20261026-1261&t=21&akid=1261%2E34582%2E9LZWnV)**
We've come too far to let up now. Let's finish the job.
I'm grateful,
Tim Walz

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/stp-ms-em-footer?refcode=em20261026-1261-&t=22&refcode2=1261_34582_9LZWnV&akid=1261%2E34582%2E9LZWnV)**

Team, thank you so much. We’re up against our most important deadline of the race at midnight tonight, and even just taking the time to read this email means a lot to me.
**[But I need to ask you to do more than read today. If you can, will you make a donation to my campaign?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142220745/656196316/-1024831887?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=email_fr_gmailnd_jtk6619&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ODI2NTY1MS01NmQxLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3B3tIoqf4G_i_SqmXbs6nsFF6moGcfaFQ6lGfL5B5s8=)** Give me a moment to explain:

The fact of the matter is that we’re being outspent on the air by the GOP. Our ads are the only way we can respond to their lies and make sure voters hear the truth before they head to the ballot box. Hey folks,
The corruption inside Trump world is starting to eat itself alive.
Trump's own Justice Department is reportedly investigating longtime ally Corey Lewandowski over whether he personally profited from his role at DHS. And Trump's response tells you everything: he keeps talking about people stealing from _him_.
* [**00:01:26**] We dig into the reported DOJ investigation of Corey Lewandowski and allegations that he personally profited while serving in a government role at DHS.
* [**00:03:44**] I explain why Trump's reaction is so revealingnand why I think loyalty, money, and the possibility of presidential pardons are central to understanding this entire ecosystem.
* [**00:06:19**] Trump reportedly starts asking questions about Lewandowski's role in a $220 million DHS advertising campaign as the fallout from Kristi Noem's tenure keeps growing.
* [**00:09:07**] We go deeper into previous reporting about Lewandowski allegedly seeking outside work while wielding enormous influence inside DHS, and the broader culture that allowed this behavior to flourish.
* [**00:11:53**] This is the part Democrats cannot forget: there's so much alleged corruption that individual scandals disappear almost immediately, and accountability has to remain a priority long after Election Day.

Corey Lewandowski is one person, but this story is about something much bigger. It's about what happens when public service becomes a vehicle for personal power and profit, and when so many scandals pile up that we stop remembering them. Case File No DRT-ED-UNDERGROUND · Special File · Three Miles Down
Power on America’s Biggest Grid Nearly Doubled in a Year. That Is Why Drilling Crews Are Working Three Miles Under the Utah Desert.
Wholesale electricity on the PJM grid went from $77.78 to $136.53 a megawatt-hour in twelve months. Oil is back above $100. September inflation re-accelerated to 3.7% on energy costs. The scarcest thing in the American economy is no longer a chip or a worker — it is a megawatt you can count on, and the search for it has gone underground.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
For twenty years, American electricity demand barely moved. Utilities planned around flat load, and nobody outside the industry thought about where the power came from. That era ended quietly, and the bill is now arriving in two places at once: the monthly statement on your kitchen table, and the capital budgets of every company that needs to plug something in.
The evidence board
| | What We Know
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the grid.** On May 14, 2026, Monitoring Analytics, the independent market monitor for PJM, reported wholesale power at $136.53 per megawatt-hour against $77.78 a year earlier — a 76% jump. The monitor laid the blame on data centers and on PJM’s failure to handle their surging demand. PJM had paused applications for new generation back in 2022, citing a years-long backlog.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the fuel.** Brent crude traded at $107.29 a barrel on October 13, 2026, after peaking at $118.35 on March 31 during the Strait of Hormuz crisis. September’s CPI came in at 3.7%, up from the summer, with energy the main driver; core inflation was 2.6%.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the new load.** In its Global Financial Stability Report of October 13, 2026, the IMF wrote that “free cash flows are rapidly declining as hyperscalers try to sustain large AI investment needs.” Translation: the companies building the data centers are now borrowing to pay for the power and the buildings around it.
| CHATTER
---
The counter-argument is worth stating. Deep projects are expensive, slow and failure-prone. Permits, water rights and local opposition kill more of them than geology does, and a resource that is abundant in the ground is not the same as a resource that is cheap at the meter.
| OUR THEORY
---
Scarcity has moved one link up the chain. For thirty years the bottleneck was the chip. Now it is the thing that makes the chip run — firm, round-the-clock power, sited where it is needed. Whoever can produce it closest to the load, and keep producing it at three in the morning, holds the asset everyone else has to buy.
Connected file
| | The Commodity Nobody Mines
---|---
There is a second way to look at this. Computing capacity itself is starting to behave like a raw material: priced, contracted years ahead, and fought over by buyers who cannot substitute anything else for it.
The numbers behind that buildout are getting heavy. One analysis of five hyperscalers — Oracle, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet — put more than $1.3 trillion of debt on their balance sheets, with roughly $3 trillion more allocated off them. The IMF flagged the same pattern in October, warning about “circular financing,” where one company funds another’s project in exchange for the money being spent on its own products.
Some analysts argue the companies supplying that capacity are the ones to watch, not the ones buying it.

The United States spent two decades treating electricity as a solved problem. It is now the constraint on the fastest-growing industry in the country, and the people with capital have noticed.

And if you know her really well, you know that even on her birthday, she'd rather be out knocking on doors, talking to voters, or finding some other way to keep busy. But I think she's earned a moment to reflect on what an extraordinary year it has been. | Last month, Kim won a hard-fought Democratic primary for Attorney General thanks to the incredible support of people like you. Since then, we've watched this campaign grow even stronger, with support from local and national advocacy organizations, Democratic groups, labor unions, elected leaders, and thousands of neighbors across our state who share Kim's vision for a safer and stronger Rhode Island. And through it all, Kim hasn't slowed down. She's been traveling across Rhode Island, meeting people where they are, listening to their concerns, and making the case for why we need an Attorney General who will fight for all of us. I've known Kim since we were students at Providence College. We actually played together on the national champion rugby team - Go Friars! We've built a life together and are raising three wonderful daughters in Providence, along with two new puppies! But one thing about Kim has never changed: when she believes in something, she gives it everything she's got. | I've seen that determination in our family, in her years as a prosecutor fighting for victims, and now in this campaign. And I couldn't be more proud of her. With Election Day just over a week away, I know exactly what Kim's birthday wish would be: to finish this campaign strong and earn the opportunity to serve Rhode Island as our next Attorney General. So I have a small birthday request of my own. I know how much your support means to Kim and how grateful she is to have you standing with her as we head into these final days. Thank you for believing in Kim and for being part of this journey. Sincerely, Jenna | P.S. Kim's closing ad is out today! Give it a watch ~~. | ~~ "Instagram" ~~ "Facebook" ~~ "Bluesky" "X" ~~ "YouTube" PAID FOR BY KIM AHERN FOR RHODE ISLAND ~ Want to change how you receive these emails? You can unsubscribe ~~.

body:
Here. Now. Today.
#
We are just about one week away from one of the most important midterm elections in modern American history.
All across the country we are going to elect candidates who will lock in the next six years of representation in the Senate, and two years of representation in the House. The final two years of Donald Trump's final term in office.
And so if we want to shape the outcome of this election it's time to hit up every auntie, every cousin, every friend, every coworker, everybody, and ask if they have turned in their ballot.
Because sometimes we make the assumption that everyone has got the message about what is going on in this country and cares as much as we do.
But people are busy. Busier now than ever. People are working two jobs now more than ever, picking up extra shifts now more than ever. It’s very easy to forget whether you mailed in your ballot or not. It’s very easy to just notch it down on the priority list between school pickup and clocking in at work. And so every single person — not only those you may convince to change their mind, but those you remind to turn out, to cast their ballot — makes a difference.
And there are so many races across the country that are just neck-and-neck.
That can be a little nerve-wracking. It can create anxiety, but the beautiful part about a neck-and-neck race is that every single choice that you make matters.
Whether it’s talking to one person, whether it’s knocking doors, every single thing you do in these final days matters. And for so many of us that have felt like our voice doesn’t matter, that our votes don’t matter, our organizing, our conversations — it matters here, it matters now, it matters today.
So talk to friends and make sure they know how to return their ballots. Ask them if they need a ride to the polls.
Volunteer to knock on doors or join a virtual phone bank from home.
Or make a donation to a candidate or organization you believe in.
[ It doesn't have to be me. But if you do want to help fund the organizers we've hired, the rallies we've held and the donations we've made, you can make a contribution to my campaign here.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261026-12472-P_FND_EXP_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12472%2E2526796%2EaJDdqI)
**[https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/contribute-to-aoc](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261026-12472-P_FND_EXP_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=12472%2E2526796%2EaJDdqI)**
**[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261026-12472-P_FND_EXP_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=23&akid=12472%2E2526796%2EaJDdqI)**
There is too much at stake to just kick up our feet and allow the outcome of this election to just happen to us. No. We all have a role of some size to play in shaping its outcome.
I intend to do my part. Thank you for joining me.
In solidarity,

clean_body: Here. Now. Today. We are just about one week away from one of the most important midterm elections in modern American history. All across the country we are going to elect candidates who will lock in the next six years of representation in the Senate, and two years of representation in the House. The final two years of Donald Trump's final term in office. And so if we want to shape the outcome of this election it's time to hit up every auntie, every cousin, every friend, every coworker, everybody, and ask if they have turned in their ballot. Because sometimes we make the assumption that everyone has got the message about what is going on in this country and cares as much as we do. But people are busy. Busier now than ever. People are working two jobs now more than ever, picking up extra shifts now more than ever. It’s very easy to forget whether you mailed in your ballot or not. It’s very easy to just notch it down on the priority list between school pickup and clocking in at work. And so every single person — not only those you may convince to change their mind, but those you remind to turn out, to cast their ballot — makes a difference. And there are so many races across the country that are just neck-and-neck. That can be a little nerve-wracking. It can create anxiety, but the beautiful part about a neck-and-neck race is that every single choice that you make matters. Whether it’s talking to one person, whether it’s knocking doors, every single thing you do in these final days matters. And for so many of us that have felt like our voice doesn’t matter, that our votes don’t matter, our organizing, our conversations — it matters here, it matters now, it matters today. So talk to friends and make sure they know how to return their ballots. Ask them if they need a ride to the polls. Volunteer to knock on doors or join a virtual phone bank from home. Or make a donation to a candidate or organization you believe in. There is too much at stake to just kick up our feet and allow the outcome of this election to just happen to us. No. We all have a role of some size to play in shaping its outcome. I intend to do my part. Thank you for joining me. In solidarity, Alexandria | ---|--- | | | ---|---|---|--- Email us: mailto: speak@ocasiocortez.com

---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 8 days. If you'd like to stop receiving emails about this contest, please [click here.](https://ak.democrats.org/signup/warren-sweepstakes-2026-opt-out/?t=2&akid=10069%2E22930333%2EngSUz-) | [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-warren-sweepstakes-2026.k_RvmO&amount=7&refcode=em_20261026_10069_fr&t=3&akid=10069%2E22930333%2EngSUz-)

Derek, with 8 days left until the midterm elections, I know it can feel like we’re running out of time.
These elections will be too close for comfort. Control of the House and Senate is going to come down to just a handful of votes in a few races. This is our chance to put a real check on Trump's power before 2028. If we win back Congress, we stop the worst of his agenda. We block his extreme judges. We hold him accountable. And we can use our power to pass plans that will actually support working people.
But we have to act now.
The DNC will have organizers on the ground, making calls, knocking doors, and protecting the vote, until these races are called. Derek, your support, and the support of grassroots Democrats just like you, is what will make that possible. **I want to meet you to say _thank you_ for being the backbone of this grassroots movement.**
[**Will you chip in $7, or any amount, to the DNC today? name: Wes Moore
subject: Saying goodbye
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2195%2E1086043%2EQjacSE)
This is a longer email about saying goodbye, Peter, but if you don’t have time to read through, I would deeply appreciate **[a contribution to power our campaign for the final week of this election.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261026-1.lcLI8f&refcode=em-20261026-1&t=2&akid=2195%2E1086043%2EQjacSE)**
After nearly a century of operation, Valley Forge Military Academy — the place where I went to school and grew from an angry, complicated child to a confident young man — has closed.
When my mother first sent me to the Forge, she saw military school as a last resort in response to a seemingly endless chain of misbehavior, both at home and at school. At age 11, I’d already felt handcuffs on my wrists. **I was not on a path to success.**
There was no overnight miracle when I started school there, but slowly, things changed. I learned about honor, code, and service. I started to take an interest in campus life, academics, and leadership positions — and I rose up the ranks and became a first captain in command of around 800 cadets.
After graduation, I went on to study at Johns Hopkins and Oxford, deployed to Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division, ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country, and now, I serve as the 63rd governor of Maryland _and the first Black governor in the history of my state._
What saddens me most isn’t losing a place I once called home. My memories will forever live on with me.
**It saddens me that other young men like me will have one fewer avenue to challenge themselves and build their own pathway to success.**
Peter, at a time where our young men and boys are falling behind and feeling isolated, we have to offer more paths for connection and engagement.
I know Valley Forge Military Academy did that for me, and I’m determined to find ways to do that for young Marylanders today.
That includes the **Maryland Corps and Service Year Option** — the first statewide program in the country to give high school graduates a year of paid, full-time community service on the path to college or a career.
We have to help young Marylanders find the thing that guides them on a pathway to success and that inspires them to serve. **[If you support that mission, I would appreciate a donation to keep me in the fight as Maryland's governor today.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261026-1.lcLI8f&refcode=em-20261026-1&t=3&akid=2195%2E1086043%2EQjacSE)**

clean_body: This is a longer email about saying goodbye, Peter, but if you don’t have time to read through, I would deeply appreciate After nearly a century of operation, Valley Forge Military Academy — the place where I went to school and grew from an angry, complicated child to a confident young man — has closed. When my mother first sent me to the Forge, she saw military school as a last resort in response to a seemingly endless chain of misbehavior, both at home and at school. At age 11, I’d already felt handcuffs on my wrists. I was not on a path to success. There was no overnight miracle when I started school there, but slowly, things changed. I learned about honor, code, and service. I started to take an interest in campus life, academics, and leadership positions — and I rose up the ranks and became a first captain in command of around 800 cadets. After graduation, I went on to study at Johns Hopkins and Oxford, deployed to Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division, ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country, and now, I serve as the 63rd governor of Maryland and the first Black governor in the history of my state. What saddens me most isn’t losing a place I once called home. My memories will forever live on with me. It saddens me that other young men like me will have one fewer avenue to challenge themselves and build their own pathway to success. Peter, at a time where our young men and boys are falling behind and feeling isolated, we have to offer more paths for connection and engagement. I know Valley Forge Military Academy did that for me, and I’m determined to find ways to do that for young Marylanders today. That includes the Maryland Corps and Service Year Option — the first statewide program in the country to give high school graduates a year of paid, full-time community service on the path to college or a career. We have to help young Marylanders find the thing that guides them on a pathway to success and that inspires them to serve. body:
[ stdin# ][IMG]

HEADLINES: Final March to the Midterms | Senate Six + 22 New House
Progressives? | Record Early Voting Nationwide + No Kings! | Flipping
Seats | Putting AIPAC on Defense | State Power | Taxing Billionaires | &
MORE!

★ ★ ★

[1]Our Revolution March to the Midterms Town Hall

THE FINAL MARCH TO THE MIDTERMS!

With just TEN DAYS to Election Day, what we do now can change the
direction of our country. Will we build a progressive future or will Trump
and the Oligarchs continue the corruption?

On Monday, Our Revolution brought together candidates and progressive
leaders on a national March to the Midterms Town Hall to organize for
VICTORY.

Our Revolution Executive Director Joseph Geevarghese laid out the stakes
and our strategy: We’re on the way to making 5 MILLION VOTER CONTACTS to
elect 6 new progressive senators and 22 additional progressives to the
House.

[2]Joseph Geevarghese Progressive Wave USA Today Quote

“It's important to recognize that the blue wave is likely to be a
progressive wave. And the incoming class of progressives has clear
demands,” Joseph told [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39922?t=1011&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]USA TODAY.

That means we must double down on voter turnout work NOW — the polls are
rosy for Democrats but pollsters warn they could be off by several points.

“We must fight like we’re 5 points down. We must out-organize the
Big Money by talking directly to voters on the phones and at the doors.”

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39923?t=1012&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]WATCH THE MARCH TO THE MIDTERMS CALL HERE

★ ★ ★

THE SUPER SENATE SIX

[5]2026 Progressive Senate Six Candidates

In ten days, we could add SIX bold new champions to join Bernie
Sanders and Chris Van Hollen in the U.S. Senate: Abdul El-Sayed in
Michigan, Troy Jackson in Maine, Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota, James
Talarico in Texas, Angie Nixon in Florida, and Charles Booker in Kentucky.

Expanding the Senate’s progressive bloc would be a game-changer for the
future of healthcare, taxes, corporate accountability, and our ability to
hold Trump and the Oligarchs accountable.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39762?t=1013&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]CHIP IN TO HELP ELECT THE SENATE SIX!

★ ★ ★

[7]Abdul for Senate Event with Chris Van Hollen

Sen. Chris Van Hollen joined Monday's call to discuss the influence of
super PACs and the policy debates that would confront a new Congress.

“This really is people-power against super PACs. It's the power of the
many against the money,” he said.

Van Hollen connected the debate over money in politics to concrete
economic issues: the cost of prescription drugs, tax advantages for
billionaires, corporate subsidies, and the growing demand for electricity
and water from AI data centers.

With leadership from Van Hollen and a growing bloc of Senate progressives,
we can shape a new future for working families. “It's not enough simply to
argue that we’ve got to return to the pre-Trump status quo.”

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39924?t=1014&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]The opportunity in front of us is enormous: flip the House and Senate,
elect a record number of progressives, and change the balance of power in
Washington. Chip in any amount for this final GOTV push!

★ ★ ★

[9]Flip the House Elect Progressives Graphic

THE POTENTIAL FOR 22 NEW HOUSE PROGRESSIVES

The Congressional Progressive Caucus has grown substantially since the
first members of the Squad entered Congress in 2018. The 2026 elections
could bring a record-breaking wave of new progressives to the House.

Rep. Becca Balint, who chairs the CPC's Ending Corporate Greed Task Force,
joined Monday’s call to explain what that could mean for the fight against
corporate power — especially if we win back control of Congress on
November 3rd.

“We have to come in swinging,” she said.

[10]Becca Balint Community Campaign Event

Balint named the targets: pharmaceutical middlemen driving up healthcare
costs, corporate consolidation, challenging powerful industries, and
getting money out of politics.

And she made clear that the current progressive bloc sees the incoming
class as important to its legislative work. “We need reinforcements.”

Some of those reinforcements joined the call, two on the cusp of flipping
red seats.

★ ★ ★

[11]Randy Villegas California 22 Campaign

THE FIGHT TO FLIP RED SEATS

In California's Central Valley, Randy Villegas is challenging Republican
Rep. David Valadao in the 22nd Congressional District.

Randy, a union teacher, has been connecting directly with families
struggling with healthcare costs, grocery bills, and the influence of
corporate donors. “Nobody should have to fight cancer and their
congressman at the same time.”

He summed up his criticism of campaign finance in one memorable line:
“Tell me who you're taking money from and I'll tell you who you're taking
orders from.”

[12]Abdul for Senate Event with Bernie Sanders

Meanwhile, in Michigan’s 7th Congressional District, Will Lawrence is
bringing his background as a climate and tenants rights organizer into his
campaign.

On Monday, Will told our movement how grateful he is to the volunteers who
have knocked nearly 200,000 doors — primarily around Lansing, MI — and the
importance of grassroots voter turnout when facing tens of millions of
outside spending.

“People are sick of the status quo,” he said. That’s why he’s fighting
data centers and giving local people a voice over their communities. But
it starts by getting involved in this election.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39925?t=1015&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]SIGN UP TO JOIN OUR PHONEBANK TEAM

★ ★ ★

[14]Melat Kiros Colorado Campaign Event

MELAT KIROS: FROM A PRIMARY UPSET TO THE NATIONAL STAGE

Colorado’s Melat Kiros had grassroots muscle behind her when she defeated
the incumbent Democrat last summer — now, she’s ready to take on the
machine in Washington DC.

“Democracy is not a spectator sport,” she told us, stressing the
importance of participating in elections as well as staying active long
after the elections are over to bring pressure to bear on decision-makers.

Melat said elected officials must be made accountable to the organizing
movements that helped bring them into office. And Our Revolution is proud
to continue our work for representation inside the Democratic Party and
elevate the role of the grassroots between elections.

★ ★ ★

[15]Aisha Wahab Our Revolution Campaign Rally

CANDIDATE SPOTLIGHT: AISHA WAHAB VS. AIPAC

Newly elected Rep. Aisha Wahab knows firsthand what it means to go up
against massive outside spending from AIPAC — and win.

After facing millions of dollars in the special election, Aisha told us
the answer isn't trying to match Big Money dollar for dollar. It's about
connecting directly with voters at the doors, on the phones, and
delivering a clear contrast to the opposition.

“Our Revolution was with us here on the ground. Real people telling
neighbors why they’re voting, what they care about, what they want to see
done — that’s really the biggest part of our campaign and how we were able
to push back.”

[16]AIPAC Ending Candidate Endorsements News Article

Significantly, AIPAC just announced it will end candidate endorsements and
direct contributions after the midterms—a retreat that reflects the
effectiveness of grassroots organizing in key races like Aisha’s and the
progressive movement’s coordinated effort to expose its right-wing agenda
and demanding accountability for enabling Israeli apartheid.

But its United Democracy Project super PAC remains active. That’s why Our
Revolution is committed to overturning Citizens United and pushing to get
the Democratic Party to ban dark and corporate money in the 2028
primaries. We need more transparency and accountabilty —not political
spending pushed further into the shadows.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39926?t=1016&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]READ MORE ABOUT OUR WORK IN THE NATION:

★ ★ ★

[18]Our Revolution Battle for the Midterms Candidates

FROM NO KINGS TO THE BALLOT BOX.

Last weekend’s No Kings demonstrations brought millions out into the
streets, but “this No Kings wasn't just about a protest,” Indivisible
co-founder Ezra Levin said on our LIVE call on Monday.

Levin reported 3,000 events nationwide to maximize early voting, local
organizing, and election-defense preparation. In ZIP codes that hosted No
Kings events, early voting was 51% higher than the same Saturday in the
last midterm election.

“The next thing is we got to actually get this vote out and protect the
vote,” Ezra continued, delving into plans for election-defense training,
community networks, and the importance of people having trusted
connections if election-related disputes arise.

“You don't have to be alone. Authoritarians want you to be alone.”

[19]Texas Record Breaking Early Voting 2026

That energy is showing up at the polls, with record-breaking turnout in
places like Dallas County, Texas, which surpassed its 2024
presidential-year opening-day total. Now we have to keep organizing to
turn those early signs of momentum into victories across the country.

★ ★ ★

[20]Our Revolution 2026 Midterms Supporter Survey

CONFIDENCE IS HIGH. COMPLACENCY IS NOT AN OPTION.

Our Revolution’s recent survey of approximately 1,500 supporters offered
another perspective on the organization's membership revealed 90% feel
confident about a blue wave.

But CNN and polling analysts like Nate Silver are warning that polling
could be skewed by up to four points in favor of Democrats — which means
we can’t rest easy.

But 90% also told us they’re concerned about possible GOP interference
with election results. We have to get out the vote and win by massive
margins to make this TOO BIG TO RIG!

While 75% said they plan to vote early, only 13% said they knew someone
planning to volunteer through phonebanking, canvassing, or helping
neighbors reach polling places.

[21]2026 Midterms Phonebank 5 Million Voter Contacts

Our Revolution activists helped make tens of thousands of calls into
Aisha's district — exactly the kind of grassroots operation we're now
scaling up across the country heading into November.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39764?t=1017&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]SIGN UP TO MAKE CALLS WITH OUR TEAM

★ ★ ★

STATE AND LOCAL RACES MAKE THE DIFFERENCE!

Three candidates joined Monday’s call and demonstrated how consequential
state and local seats can be for economic policy, civil rights, and more.

[23]Eli Savit Michigan Attorney General Rally

ELI SAVIT: THE ATTORNEY GENERAL'S POWER TO TAKE ON CORPORATE WRONGDOING

Michigan Attorney General candidate Eli Savit explained why the office is
much more than the state’s top prosecutor.

A former environmental lawyer and Our Revolution endorsed county
prosecutor, Savit discussed litigation against polluters, the opioid
industry, and other powerful interests — and the importance of state AGs
in defending election administration and constitutional rights.

“The state attorney general is the one actor that can go into court on
behalf of the entire people of their state,” he said. This is especially
important, he noted, as Michigan is poised to be one of the hotly
contested early primary states in the 2028 presidential cycle.

★ ★ ★

[24]Vikki Goodwin Texas Campaign Rally

VIKKI GOODWIN: BUILDING THE FIGHT IN TEXAS

Our Revolution endorsed Texas State Rep. Vikki Goodwin is running for
Lieutenant Governor, a key role in the Lone Star State that has
extraordinary influence over the Texas Senate's legislative agenda.

Goodwin described long early-voting lines, public concern about school
vouchers and utility bills, and growing questions about the resources
required by large data centers.

“Data centers have come up an awful lot because of the vast amounts of
water and energy that these data centers will use,” she said.

★ ★ ★

[25]Kennedy Moore Missouri House Campaign Event

KENNEDY MOORE: DEFENDING THE WILL OF THE VOTERS

Missouri House District 73 candidate Kennedy Moore brought a background in
Ferguson activism, student organizing, and reproductive justice to the
call. She’s part of a slate of Our Revolution-backed candidates running
to break the GOP supermajority in the State Capitol.

“There’s a common theme of our politicians undermining the will of the
people,” Kennedy said, and that conflict is also directly connected to
several measures on Missouri’s November ballot that we’re organizing to
win!

[26]Missouri Ballot Measures Amendment 6 3 Prop A

YES ON AMENDMENT 6 to strengthen protections for Missouri's initiative and
referendum process — preventing lawmakers from weakening certain petition
rules.

NO ON AMENDMENT 3 to protect reproductive freedom, including abortion
access and protect gender-transition medical procedures for minors.

NO ON PROPOSITION A to reject Republicans’ gerrymandered congressional
map.

★ ★ ★

CALIFORNIA BALLOT MEASURES: TAX BILLIONAIRES. EXPAND DEMOCRACY.

[27]California Billionaire Tax Act Graphic

Speaking of ballot measures, Our Revolution is also mobilizing our

1 MILLION SUPPORTERS in California support two measures that will directly
challenge the political power of the billionaire class:

VOTE YES ON PROP 40 — The California Billionaires Tax Act would raise $100
billion with a one-time 5% wealth tax and would help replace lost federal
funding and protect critical programs. All without a dime of extra taxes
on the middle class or small businesses.

YES ON PROP 4 to remove the California prohibition on public
campaign-financing and allow local governments to establish programs with
eligibility rules and spending restrictions.

★ ★ ★

[28]Our Revolution Get Out the Vote Canvassing

FIVE MILLION VOTER CONTACTS. HELP US FINISH THE JOB.

We’re more than halfway toward our goal of five million voter contacts.
Now we need to turn that work into victories.

Our Revolution's national field operation set a goal of five million voter
contacts in the midterms — and we’re HALFWAY THERE!

The operation includes phonebanking, texting, canvassing, emailing,
volunteer recruitment, and coordination with campaigns and local
organizers.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39763?t=1018&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]We’re on a mission to add even more phonebanks in these last 10 days.
Donate $5, $10, or $27 to our Midterms Battle Fund to support this work in
the final homestretch to Election Day!

★ ★ ★

[30]Our Revolution Ten Years Fight Oligarchy Banner

10 YEARS OF BUILDING POWER. 10 DAYS TIL ELECTION DAY. LET’S FLEX IT.

Bernie Sanders founded Our Revolution in 2016 to take on the corporate
class and empower everyday people. In 10 years, we’ve helped elect more
than 1,200 progressives at every level of government.

Our movement is taking on Trump, the oligarchs, and the Democratic
establishment. Progressives aren’t just winning primaries. We’re building
the infrastructure, mobilizing turnout, and powering the blue wave.

[31]Joseph Geevarghese Vote Blue OpEd Graphic

If we deliver the candidates, organizers, and voters, who's actually the
power in the party?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39927?t=1019&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]READ OUR LATEST OPED IN COMMON DREAMS.

★ ★ ★

[33]Our Revolution 2026 Midterms Phonebank Zoom Call

It’s all hands on deck — and on the phones. It’s a lot of fun and it’s the
best way to make the biggest impact on these Midterms. Sign up today!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39764?t=1020&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]JOIN OUR PHONE BANK FORCE

★ ★ ★

[35]Make Trump Cry No Kings Sticker Merch

It’s time to Make Trump Cry in the Midterms!

Let’s take power back from Trump and the oligarchs who are entrenching us
in war, rigging our economy, and targeting our communities. Get your
[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39768?t=1021&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]stickers and other merch to help power our organizing. Thanks for all
of your support!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37510?t=1022&akid=11501%2E5885482%2EBzBL_l ]GRAB YOUR MERCH!

With leadership from Van Hollen and a growing bloc of Senate progressives, we can shape a new future for working families. “It's not enough simply to argue that we’ve got to return to the pre-Trump status quo.” [ ]The opportunity in front of us is enormous: flip the House and Senate, elect a record number of progressives, and change the balance of power in Washington. Chip in any amount for this final GOTV push! ★ ★ ★ [9]Flip the House Elect Progressives Graphic THE POTENTIAL FOR 22 NEW HOUSE PROGRESSIVES The Congressional Progressive Caucus has grown substantially since the first members of the Squad entered Congress in 2018. The 2026 elections could bring a record-breaking wave of new progressives to the House. Rep. Becca Balint, who chairs the CPC's Ending Corporate Greed Task Force, joined Monday’s call to explain what that could mean for the fight against corporate power — especially if we win back control of Congress on November 3rd. “We have to come in swinging,” she said. [10]Becca Balint Community Campaign Event Balint named the targets: pharmaceutical middlemen driving up healthcare costs, corporate consolidation, challenging powerful industries, and getting money out of politics. And she made clear that the current progressive bloc sees the incoming class as important to its legislative work. “We need reinforcements.” Some of those reinforcements joined the call, two on the cusp of flipping red seats. ★ ★ ★ [11]Randy Villegas California 22 Campaign THE FIGHT TO FLIP RED SEATS In California's Central Valley, Randy Villegas is challenging Republican Rep. David Valadao in the 22nd Congressional District. Randy, a union teacher, has been connecting directly with families struggling with healthcare costs, grocery bills, and the influence of corporate donors. “Nobody should have to fight cancer and their congressman at the same time.” He summed up his criticism of campaign finance in one memorable line: “Tell me who you're taking money from and I'll tell you who you're taking orders from.” [12]Abdul for Senate Event with Bernie Sanders Meanwhile, in Michigan’s 7th Congressional District, Will Lawrence is bringing his background as a climate and tenants rights organizer into his campaign. On Monday, Will told our movement how grateful he is to the volunteers who have knocked nearly 200,000 doors — primarily around Lansing, MI — and the importance of grassroots voter turnout when facing tens of millions of outside spending. “People are sick of the status quo,” he said. That’s why he’s fighting data centers and giving local people a voice over their communities. But it starts by getting involved in this election. [ ]SIGN UP TO JOIN OUR PHONEBANK TEAM ★ ★ ★ [14]Melat Kiros Colorado Campaign Event MELAT KIROS: FROM A PRIMARY UPSET TO THE NATIONAL STAGE Colorado’s Melat Kiros had grassroots muscle behind her when she defeated the incumbent Democrat last summer — now, she’s ready to take on the machine in Washington DC. “Democracy is not a spectator sport,” she told us, stressing the importance of participating in elections as well as staying active long after the elections are over to bring pressure to bear on decision-makers. Melat said elected officials must be made accountable to the organizing movements that helped bring them into office. And Our Revolution is proud to continue our work for representation inside the Democratic Party and elevate the role of the grassroots between elections. ★ ★ ★ [15]Aisha Wahab Our Revolution Campaign Rally CANDIDATE SPOTLIGHT: AISHA WAHAB VS. AIPAC Newly elected Rep. Aisha Wahab knows firsthand what it means to go up against massive outside spending from AIPAC — and win. After facing millions of dollars in the special election, Aisha told us the answer isn't trying to match Big Money dollar for dollar. It's about connecting directly with voters at the doors, on the phones, and delivering a clear contrast to the opposition. “Our Revolution was with us here on the ground. Real people telling neighbors why they’re voting, what they care about, what they want to see done — that’s really the biggest part of our campaign and how we were able to push back.” [16]AIPAC Ending Candidate Endorsements News Article Significantly, AIPAC just announced it will end candidate endorsements and direct contributions after the midterms—a retreat that reflects the effectiveness of grassroots organizing in key races like Aisha’s and the progressive movement’s coordinated effort to expose its right-wing agenda and demanding accountability for enabling Israeli apartheid. But its United Democracy Project super PAC remains active. That’s why Our Revolution is committed to overturning Citizens United and pushing to get the Democratic Party to ban dark and corporate money in the 2028 primaries. We need more transparency and accountabilty —not political spending pushed further into the shadows. [ ]READ MORE ABOUT OUR WORK IN THE NATION: ★ ★ ★ [18]Our Revolution Battle for the Midterms Candidates FROM NO KINGS TO THE BALLOT BOX. Last weekend’s No Kings demonstrations brought millions out into the streets, but “this No Kings wasn't just about a protest,” Indivisible co-founder Ezra Levin said on our LIVE call on Monday. Levin reported 3,000 events nationwide to maximize early voting, local organizing, and election-defense preparation. In ZIP codes that hosted No Kings events, early voting was 51% higher than the same Saturday in the last midterm election. “The next thing is we got to actually get this vote out and protect the vote,” Ezra continued, delving into plans for election-defense training, community networks, and the importance of people having trusted connections if election-related disputes arise. “You don't have to be alone. Authoritarians want you to be alone.” [19]Texas Record Breaking Early Voting 2026 That energy is showing up at the polls, with record-breaking turnout in places like Dallas County, Texas, which surpassed its 2024 presidential-year opening-day total. Now we have to keep organizing to turn those early signs of momentum into victories across the country. ★ ★ ★ [20]Our Revolution 2026 Midterms Supporter Survey CONFIDENCE IS HIGH. COMPLACENCY IS NOT AN OPTION. Our Revolution’s recent survey of approximately 1,500 supporters offered another perspective on the organization's membership revealed 90% feel confident about a blue wave. But CNN and polling analysts like Nate Silver are warning that polling could be skewed by up to four points in favor of Democrats — which means we can’t rest easy. But 90% also told us they’re concerned about possible GOP interference with election results. We have to get out the vote and win by massive margins to make this TOO BIG TO RIG! While 75% said they plan to vote early, only 13% said they knew someone planning to volunteer through phonebanking, canvassing, or helping neighbors reach polling places. [21]2026 Midterms Phonebank 5 Million Voter Contacts Our Revolution activists helped make tens of thousands of calls into Aisha's district — exactly the kind of grassroots operation we're now scaling up across the country heading into November. [ ]SIGN UP TO MAKE CALLS WITH OUR TEAM ★ ★ ★ STATE AND LOCAL RACES MAKE THE DIFFERENCE! Three candidates joined Monday’s call and demonstrated how consequential state and local seats can be for economic policy, civil rights, and more. [23]Eli Savit Michigan Attorney General Rally ELI SAVIT: THE ATTORNEY GENERAL'S POWER TO TAKE ON CORPORATE WRONGDOING Michigan Attorney General candidate Eli Savit explained why the office is much more than the state’s top prosecutor. A former environmental lawyer and Our Revolution endorsed county prosecutor, Savit discussed litigation against polluters, the opioid industry, and other powerful interests — and the importance of state AGs in defending election administration and constitutional rights. “The state attorney general is the one actor that can go into court on behalf of the entire people of their state,” he said. This is especially important, he noted, as Michigan is poised to be one of the hotly contested early primary states in the 2028 presidential cycle. ★ ★ ★ [24]Vikki Goodwin Texas Campaign Rally VIKKI GOODWIN: BUILDING THE FIGHT IN TEXAS Our Revolution endorsed Texas State Rep. Vikki Goodwin is running for Lieutenant Governor, a key role in the Lone Star State that has extraordinary influence over the Texas Senate's legislative agenda. Goodwin described long early-voting lines, public concern about school vouchers and utility bills, and growing questions about the resources required by large data centers. “Data centers have come up an awful lot because of the vast amounts of water and energy that these data centers will use,” she said. ★ ★ ★ [25]Kennedy Moore Missouri House Campaign Event KENNEDY MOORE: DEFENDING THE WILL OF THE VOTERS Missouri House District 73 candidate Kennedy Moore brought a background in Ferguson activism, student organizing, and reproductive justice to the call. She’s part of a slate of Our Revolution-backed candidates running to break the GOP supermajority in the State Capitol. “There’s a common theme of our politicians undermining the will of the people,” Kennedy said, and that conflict is also directly connected to several measures on Missouri’s November ballot that we’re organizing to win! [26]Missouri Ballot Measures Amendment 6 3 Prop A YES ON AMENDMENT 6 to strengthen protections for Missouri's initiative and referendum process — preventing lawmakers from weakening certain petition rules. NO ON AMENDMENT 3 to protect reproductive freedom, including abortion access and protect gender-transition medical procedures for minors. NO ON PROPOSITION A to reject Republicans’ gerrymandered congressional map. ★ ★ ★ CALIFORNIA BALLOT MEASURES: TAX BILLIONAIRES. EXPAND DEMOCRACY. [27]California Billionaire Tax Act Graphic Speaking of ballot measures, Our Revolution is also mobilizing our 1 MILLION SUPPORTERS in California support two measures that will directly challenge the political power of the billionaire class: VOTE YES ON PROP 40 — The California Billionaires Tax Act would raise $100 billion with a one-time 5% wealth tax and would help replace lost federal funding and protect critical programs. All without a dime of extra taxes on the middle class or small businesses. YES ON PROP 4 to remove the California prohibition on public campaign-financing and allow local governments to establish programs with eligibility rules and spending restrictions. ★ ★ ★ [28]Our Revolution Get Out the Vote Canvassing FIVE MILLION VOTER CONTACTS. HELP US FINISH THE JOB. We’re more than halfway toward our goal of five million voter contacts. Now we need to turn that work into victories. Our Revolution's national field operation set a goal of five million voter contacts in the midterms — and we’re HALFWAY THERE! The operation includes phonebanking, texting, canvassing, emailing, volunteer recruitment, and coordination with campaigns and local organizers. [ ]We’re on a mission to add even more phonebanks in these last 10 days. Donate $5, $10, or $27 to our Midterms Battle Fund to support this work in the final homestretch to Election Day! ★ ★ ★ [30]Our Revolution Ten Years Fight Oligarchy Banner 10 YEARS OF BUILDING POWER. 10 DAYS TIL ELECTION DAY. LET’S FLEX IT. Bernie Sanders founded Our Revolution in 2016 to take on the corporate class and empower everyday people. In 10 years, we’ve helped elect more than 1,200 progressives at every level of government. Our movement is taking on Trump, the oligarchs, and the Democratic establishment. Progressives aren’t just winning primaries. We’re building the infrastructure, mobilizing turnout, and powering the blue wave. David is the Milwaukee County Executive, a lifelong public servant, and someone who knows firsthand what working families are up against.
#
Peter,
I'm proud to endorse David Crowley for governor of Wisconsin.
David is the Milwaukee County Executive, a lifelong public servant, and someone who knows firsthand what working families are up against. With just eight days until Election Day, Trump's MAGA megadonor allies are doing everything they can to tear him down and drown out his message.
**[Will you split a donation between David's campaign and Small Town PAC today to help him fight back against these attacks and power his campaign across the finish line?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-partner-dc-20261026-1.-iSqAo&amount=5&refcode=em20261026-1262&t=1&akid=1262%2E34582%2EKjzkjz)**
David grew up in Milwaukee, where his parents struggled with addiction and mental health challenges. There were times when his family didn't know if the bills would get paid or if there would be enough food on the table.
Those experiences shaped who he is today. David understands what happens when the systems families depend on fail them, because he's lived it. And as Milwaukee County Executive, he's worked to make those systems better, from expanding mental health services to investing in affordable housing.
Now, he's running for governor to lower costs, strengthen public schools, improve access to affordable health care, and make sure communities across Wisconsin aren't left behind.
**That's the kind of work David wants to take statewide. But with just eight days left, we need to make sure Wisconsin voters hear his message before they head to the polls.**
**[Peter, will you join me in supporting David by splitting $5 or whatever works for you between his campaign and Small Town PAC? Tim

name: Adam Schiff
subject: A very honest email about the importance of small-dollar donations
body:
| Peter, this is Adam Schiff. I know you've been getting a lot of emails from me (and other candidates) ahead of the upcoming election. But please hear me out. I want to try something different today and take a moment to explain the importance of small grassroots contributions to our operation. Trump has personally made more than $2.2 billion in income since returning to the White House, and his agenda has sent a clear, unmistakable message about who this administration works for: billionaires first, you last. **Now he and his billionaire allies are pouring money into the midterms to protect the Republicans in Congress who enable their self-dealing.** They know we are on track to flip control of the House and the Senate, and they know that when we do — when the gavels and subpoena power finally change hands — we will expose and investigate their corrupt schemes. body:
This is a long but critically important read.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Hi Peter, it's Gina.
Everywhere I go in Texas, I hear the same thing: people are struggling in ways they've never struggled before. Working people donating plasma before their shift just to cover the bills. Families rationing insulin. Small businesses closing because property taxes have gotten so out of hand.
And everywhere I go, I hear something else too:_that this movement is giving them hope_. We’re closer than we’ve ever been before, but we have a long way to go. People still worry if we can actually win here.
I understand that skepticism. Democrats have been saying Texas is turning for years. **But something is different now, and I need you to see the numbers.**
My campaign manager Amy put together a memo on exactly where this race stands. Six independent polls now show us ahead. Abbott's own strategist is admitting it will be close. Conservatives across Texas are crossing over — on schools, on data centers, on the simple question of whether this state belongs to the people or to Greg Abbott's billionaire donors.
**[Read the memo. Then, if you believe what I believe — that we can actually win this — I'm asking you to pitch in whatever you can.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261026_2_memo._0Qqh2&refcode=em20261026-2547&t=1&akid=2547%2E299639%2EL_JJmZ)**
[Donate »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261026_2_memo._0Qqh2&refcode=em20261026-2547&t=2&akid=2547%2E299639%2EL_JJmZ)
=============================================================
**OCTOBER 2026 CAMPAIGN MEMO ON TX-GOV**
**FROM:** Amy Friedman, Campaign Manager, Gina for Texas
**TO:** Interested Parties
Let me tell you where this race actually stands — because what's happening in Texas right now is something I don't think the national establishment fully understands yet.

**Gina Hinojosa is leading Greg Abbott in six of the most recent polls. That’s never happened before.**
This race is closer than ever but some people still don’t believe we can win — that’s exactly why I'm writing this memo. And it's exactly why this race could slip away if we don't act.
Here's the polling picture. This race has moved steadily and dramatically in Gina's direction since the spring:
* Texas Politics Project (April 2026): Abbott +5
* TPOR (July 2026): Abbott +3, inside the margin of error
* N+ Univision (September 9): Tied 47–47, with Gina leading Latino voters by 12
* ReconMR/Siena (September 17): **Gina leads 49–45** — independents breaking for Gina 65–27
* NPR/Marist (September 23): **Gina leads 49–46** , winning independents 52–39, pulling 9% of self-identified Republicans
* NYT/Siena (October 4):**Gina leads 49–46** , winning independents 55–39, and leading among Latino voters by 31 points
* YouGov (October 2026): **Gina +1**
* GBAO Poll (October 13): **Gina +2**
* UT/Texas Politics Project (October 14): **Gina +1**

Both RealClearPolitics and Nate Silver's Silver Bulletin have the polling average under 3 points. This is a toss-up.
**Abbott is outspending us 10 to 1 — and he still isn’t getting the result he wants.**
Between July 30 and September 8 alone, Abbott outspent Gina $28 million to $2 million on advertising. Over the full race, he's spent $47 million to our $5 million. Despite that, Gina leads in six of the most recent polls. Abbott's favorability has gone deeply negative — 45% favorable, 53% unfavorable — and his job approval has flipped the same way. He's even polling 13% unfavorable among his own Republicans.
Abbott is a damaged incumbent with a nine-figure war chest. The only thing keeping this race from breaking open is the spending gap.
But here’s the truth: The more money Abbott spends lying about Gina’s record, the more vulnerable we are. _We have to raise more money to reach the voters who haven’t heard from us yet._
**Something real is happening on the ground — and Republicans know it.**
Lifelong conservative voters are publicly breaking with Abbott over two issues.
On education: conservative moms who backed Abbott before are now appearing at Gina's events, frustrated by a decade of voucher schemes and defunded public schools. Gina is running an ad featuring a self-described MAGA conservative who protested on January 6 — and is now voting for Gina because of schools.
On data centers: rural Republican protest groups — including one in Lubbock led by Republicans — are furious about unregulated expansion driving up electricity bills. Abbott championed data centers for years, took millions from their developers, and is now scrambling to reverse course. Gina called for a moratorium from day one.
As Gina put it to The Nation: The data-center issue is the latest example of a governor doing the bidding of moneyed interests and not the people of Texas. And it is angering MAGA Republicans — not country-club Republicans, not Chamber of Commerce Republicans. There is an opportunity for alliances to be forged when we are pursuing a populist agenda.
**Even Abbott's own team is admitting this race is close.**
Abbott's longtime political strategist was asked about the tightening polls. His response: "Is it going to be close on Election Day? Yes." That’s Abbott's own guy publicly conceding this goes to the wire. And when pressed on his best argument against Gina? He went to culture wars and lies on income tax votes — not data centers, not schools, not the affordability crisis Abbott has presided over for twelve years. When culture wars are the best attack you can come up with, you're losing ground.
**The coalition winning this race doesn't look like past Texas Democratic coalitions.**
Gina leads independents by 38 points in the Siena poll. She's winning women 57–40%, voters under 45 by 60–33%, and Gen Z 71–19%. She's pulling 9% of self-identified Republicans. In TX-15 — a district Trump carried 58–41 — a House Majority PAC poll shows Gina leading 52–47.
This is a cross-partisan, cross-regional majority being built in real time. _Gina is earning support from Texans who have never voted for a Democrat before in their lives._
**When Texas Democrats run strong, the whole map shifts.**
In 2018, when Beto lost the Senate race by just 2.6 points, that wave energy flipped 12 State House seats, 2 State Senate seats, and 2 congressional seats. And the stakes this cycle go even further: if Abbott wins another term, Republicans will redraw the congressional map again. body:
We can’t let this momentum slip away.
#
Take a look at this map, Peter:
[](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20261026-1.6x5Oj6&amount=3&refcode=em20261026-718&t=1&akid=718%2E1366028%2ER2hr2G)
Texans are showing up, Peter. In just the first few days of early voting, **4,251,983 Texans have already cast their ballots.** That’s millions of people who’ve decided they’re done waiting for change and are ready to make it happen themselves.
**But here’s what this map doesn’t show yet — whether Latino voters are turning out in the numbers it takes to transform Texas. From the Rio Grande Valley to San Antonio to Houston to Dallas, our communities have the power to decide who leads this state — but only if we show up.**
Early voting ends October 30, and every day between now and then counts. That’s why we’re on the ground across Texas, knocking on doors, sharing accurate election information, and making sure every eligible Latino voter knows where, when, and how to vote.
Peter, we can’t let this momentum slip away. **[Will you chip in $3 or any amount today to help us reach Latino voters across Texas before Election Day?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20261026-1.6x5Oj6&amount=3&refcode=em20261026-718&t=2&akid=718%2E1366028%2ER2hr2G)**

name: Newt Gingrich
subject: I have been involved in three really disruptive moments in American politics. This is the fourth.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the NRSC
body:
I have been a first-hand witness to three disruptive moments in American politics. What I am watching build right now may be the fourth — and unlike the others, this one could go either way. | Fellow American,

I have been involved in three really disruptive moments in American politics.

The first was Ronald Reagan in the late seventies and early eighties. People thought he was a cowboy who did not know what he was doing. Nine years later, the Soviet Union disappeared. That was a disruption.

The second was 1994, when I helped lead Republicans to the first House majority in forty years. We had a Contract with America. We had candidates who signed it. We had a grassroots base that understood exactly what was at stake. And we won because we did the organizing work before the election, not after it.

The third is Donald Trump, a disruptor whose legacy, I have said publicly, may rival the most consequential presidents in American history if the 2026 midterms go well for Republicans.

**_[Fellow American, that last part is the one I need to talk to you about.](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=f1a79478a1cc4710a9a0d78fc0d1ff19&_e=6xkO9fCkwl_6OpRxH4t983sWHLt5l0QCCzxNxj4VfHMAeLNwhdgFS_xRyvZaSbF5eAG9dESje63s8DFUBDCJGUgSLyJrnewBGpgKly6Wtd1D-1Kk5x7NHhbL07HQl5eXUdr4evfEDxu0Rwx97CW7X8E757BeehT3mB5f1on7zQ3L8wM-jPs4QR8RjnO-eL3T5J_2gElRXCO3LrqwpgM6xTlSsZpnXH4g6SVk_I8u0XyjjmuJiGtNynbhi42OUmuc3LPI9VO8Jw4AoLKvNDxlt_sY00FYwGvryrDFzjsK1aOxwsWcgWb5dMQXnL6yTkj5fUYuLYbXmHXhL8LMEGC4ca_dNtfM2_wbq6fUEXMcW0ePe_sYyXUzHMj2Zdww4zFmpZS8I7swi5Ap9Ns5yNq9uB1Cd61mJiZVz5X4P-E4AOuk0QDqCMkjmTeCnfB8pYWHr_zz0pkWAQleGHh-OEOX7l2Y8aDy-nKkBxLzWx7BQ1DplAeivyJYgsQ3MfXNblkUiVIe8yjJn7pYgzFdmedpWCI57dD3OIWUlKm_SJdYNL61e0QPh3ZdhawtAYBCynJjEgK4XWOnLPgFDllWHJHmqRuMKgyDqIiP1d440OBDC1nuU8jdwc6CxOS7fnO3GS5FvmvFgRmXm8ftF_35ZP-fxSc5nQBBP1jHwiwPrD48Afoi8JVOxguTy__XX7W9yzv2TZfDejCtrONoDhK0OLMFNE-V0AF2NYRgqHByEjQLygFkevcKxLsxfBgxpGahfCoOESAXST_ExKZjA3sI9_E7wtRluxONpoNpZyx1J58KIrO-GO_4FebujnvuS6N6rLnyr8SDKsgX0SDJi5SqIoVvKnIsQ0NnZO2r9OTogjMYKOXRnFC85T1JC8DdoL1fPH4kt1Y-GhBhIzXavmONOMKED1wAW8GqEGAVgrswXTzfIXtySSvI7FhN2jcG1Rp7GJkQWDvfRlAmKZt-ctEn7GMOXpOeH9bLhDRjsKEWfv4r86reXFVu20wt-wO7vHFx33zW760Vt_NRgiSucRFaXNqB1lsY_MjPVvvZeBCpj0Y3HZcwsy5iuaG-BurAM19rAdLF-xMisw7RLgJvKCLKCfXYyA%3D%3D)_ **

I have watched majorities built and I have watched them collapse. I know what the organization looks like when it succeeds and I know what it looks like when it quietly falls apart. And right now, in the Senate races that will determine whether President Trump has a working legislative majority for the next two years, I am seeing something that concerns me.

**[The DSA is no longer fringe.](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=f1a79478a1cc4710a9a0d78fc0d1ff19&_e=6xkO9fCkwl_6OpRxH4t983sWHLt5l0QCCzxNxj4VfHMAeLNwhdgFS_xRyvZaSbF5eAG9dESje63s8DFUBDCJGUgSLyJrnewBGpgKly6Wtd1D-1Kk5x7NHhbL07HQl5eXUdr4evfEDxu0Rwx97CW7X8E757BeehT3mB5f1on7zQ3L8wM-jPs4QR8RjnO-eL3T5J_2gElRXCO3LrqwpgM6xTlSsZpnXH4g6SVk_I8u0XyjjmuJiGtNynbhi42OUmuc3LPI9VO8Jw4AoLKvNDxlt_sY00FYwGvryrDFzjsK1aOxwsWcgWb5dMQXnL6yTkj5fUYuLYbXmHXhL8LMEGC4ca_dNtfM2_wbq6fUEXMcW0ePe_sYyXUzHMj2Zdww4zFmpZS8I7swi5Ap9Ns5yNq9uB1Cd61mJiZVz5X4P-E4AOuk0QDqCMkjmTeCnfB8pYWHaQl6U25KdQpa5Ne0f-SASREzzkaVPW7Sl-AtgVuYKNUl79UxS6uJ5ZVPMoXCyoGsWZMqdgi_TLvBczZ6sXJcxEwh2VN7bsAlAhLfTXOO2u0DO94zs3ne6QGb9_h4gNrbi42oby5aK1A2lFSKxdnoshPGIbdmqizkR3hl2k6vYncEEnWdbqzgdYF6TuZT9zWFTRsJriVLJPgII5J0bUWFY_81uogAl-Kjg4zBRS0rXNmlLAmqakKeuacUof1uRa7vj98yDtatHRYYmhswcfcrulbopXChQxDbKDQEPFA9DGeazONZXC7JfRAXu97LINADkyiMgezm6GxaolCdgts732gSkK3ryS310UJjUUSOicIGm3d2oN-3QmMW4et9cDXuiN2Y_O1x_twzH45qJv7C0337uAlCsqdP6tid8eKSEzAub3QkuaFUV6wJmDol5WWAQUBoG8hE1g2fzbb0IDy1KN5q-lqzr8ZD0d6UGG8CFD9zawXFfNXrk5rWLpLntZnJV2xhUmPhjnvfsUp1tTfEs5aRmm6pGoT2cj8JbilPkjDWZ1zMtYuRgoRKYvG7pM2BybbAIH8h0nYQj2nhyH4TA6qKhD_MLriodorJt-wsqjvXIwIHHP5THQTgwixvKmKLNDnPXGCSM5fnEXsX-cIxwg%3D%3D)** They are winning primaries in Michigan. They are running in states we have not had to defend in a generation. Their candidates are going into November better funded than ours in Texas, Iowa, North Carolina, and Georgia.

History teaches us that those who refuse to learn from its lessons are doomed to repeat them. I have spent sixty years learning these lessons. The lesson right now is that organized, funded conservatives win Senate majorities. Complacent ones hand them to Chuck Schumer.

clean_body: I have been a first-hand witness to three disruptive moments in American politics. What I am watching build right now may be the fourth — and unlike the others, this one could go either way. | Fellow American, I have been involved in three really disruptive moments in American politics. The first was Ronald Reagan in the late seventies and early eighties. People thought he was a cowboy who did not know what he was doing. Nine years later, the Soviet Union disappeared. That was a disruption. The second was 1994, when I helped lead Republicans to the first House majority in forty years. We had a Contract with America. We had candidates who signed it. We had a grassroots base that understood exactly what was at stake. And we won because we did the organizing work before the election, not after it. The third is Donald Trump, a disruptor whose legacy, I have said publicly, may rival the most consequential presidents in American history if the 2026 midterms go well for Republicans. I have watched majorities built and I have watched them collapse. I know what the organization looks like when it succeeds and I know what it looks like when it quietly falls apart. And right now, in the Senate races that will determine whether President Trump has a working legislative majority for the next two years, I am seeing something that concerns me. They are winning primaries in Michigan. They are running in states we have not had to defend in a generation. Their candidates are going into November better funded than ours in Texas, Iowa, North Carolina, and Georgia. History teaches us that those who refuse to learn from its lessons are doomed to repeat them. I have spent sixty years learning these lessons. The lesson right now is that organized, funded conservatives win Senate majorities. Complacent ones hand them to Chuck Schumer. If I were a Democrat right now, I would feel very confident heading into November. I am not going to let that confidence be justified. _**The weak department?**_ I enlisted in the Marine Corps right out of high school. I made sergeant, then spent decades in the Army and retired as a Brigadier General. After 9/11, I led infantry soldiers in combat in Afghanistan. In 2014, I took a team into Liberia while Ebola was killing thousands, because that was the mission and somebody had to go. **I never served with a single weak person in 40 years.** Not the young soldiers who walked patrols knowing what could be waiting for them. Not the medics, mechanics, and cooks who kept us alive and moving. Not the military families who held everything together at home while we were gone. So who does Pete Hegseth think he is? **Our armed forces have never been weak. Not under any president or any party. Those men and women were strong long before he got a podium, and they'll be strong long after he's gone.** Northwest Georgia is full of veterans and military families who know that truth. They deserve a representative who will stand up and say it proudly. Right now, Clay Fuller holds this seat, and I haven't heard him say a word. On November 3, I'm asking voters to send someone to Congress who knows what our troops are made of, because I served with them. **We have 29 days left. Every dollar helps us get this message on TV screens, in mailboxes, and on veterans' doors across the district before Election Day. So I am asking: Can you chip in $25 right now to send a veteran to Congress who will stand up to Pete Hegseth?**

clean_body: | | Pete Hegseth stood in front of our service members and said this: "We are no longer the woke department or the weak department." | The weak department? I enlisted in the Marine Corps right out of high school. I made sergeant, then spent decades in the Army and retired as a Brigadier General. After 9/11, I led infantry soldiers in combat in Afghanistan. In 2014, I took a team into Liberia while Ebola was killing thousands, because that was the mission and somebody had to go. I never served with a single weak person in 40 years. Not the young soldiers who walked patrols knowing what could be waiting for them. Not the medics, mechanics, and cooks who kept us alive and moving. Not the military families who held everything together at home while we were gone. So who does Pete Hegseth think he is? Our armed forces have never been weak. Not under any president or any party. Those men and women were strong long before he got a podium, and they'll be strong long after he's gone. Northwest Georgia is full of veterans and military families who know that truth. They deserve a representative who will stand up and say it proudly. Right now, Clay Fuller holds this seat, and I haven't heard him say a word. On November 3, I'm asking voters to send someone to Congress who knows what our troops are made of, because I served with them. We have 29 days left. Every dollar helps us get this message on TV screens, in mailboxes, and on veterans' doors across the district before Election Day. So I am asking: Can you chip in $25 right now to send a veteran to Congress who will stand up to Pete Hegseth? ~~ ~~ - Thank you, Ret. → Wisconsin would be led by **one of the MOST conservative Wisconsin House members in modern history**.
→ Our state will be at the whim of Donald Trump and his millionaire friends – **not Wisconsin families.**

---
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142230152/656223711/-373287771?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_261026_FR_WildestDream_A0_na_U1_X2_M1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYWQwYzY0Ni02NGQxLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3qDioRUsWLIHQLC5X68ufXq2k5niZg8r6baWFWSXiK0=) I remember the exact moment this photo was taken. It was 1993, my Induction Day at the Naval Academy. I was so proud to be there, with the chance to learn, work, and see the world in service of my country. **The young woman in this photo had no idea what was coming.** She never imagined she’d be a member of Congress. She never imagined she’d be inside the Capitol when it came under siege for the first time since the War of 1812. She never imagined running for her life from a violent mob, or evacuating her office because someone had planted a pipe bomb outside. She expected danger when she joined the Navy. But it didn’t come from enemy ships or submarines. It came from the most unthinkable place: the Commander-in-Chief. I served on the January 6th Committee knowing it could cost me my seat. It did. I’d do it again, for her. # [Brazilian stocks crater after left-wing Lula's fourth-term win](https://substack.com/redirect/83303b85-3ae6-4b99-a16f-3e053b026c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Brazilian **[ADRs plunged premarket Monday](https://substack.com/redirect/7fa58e07-f590-46c1-8b54-9be17b7418de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/35884229-80b8-4121-8f93-c88aaeda3302?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a historic fourth term with 51.8% of the vote,](https://substack.com/redirect/35884229-80b8-4121-8f93-c88aaeda3302?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/35884229-80b8-4121-8f93-c88aaeda3302?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)reversing bets on a Flavio Bolsonaro victory and prompting calls to annul the runoff.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/83303b85-3ae6-4b99-a16f-3e053b026c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **XP sinks 52% premarket** : Other Brazil-exposed names fell hard, including Nu Holdings down about 22-25%, Petrobras off roughly 21%, and the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF sharply lower overnight.
* **First runoff comeback since 1989** : Lula overcame a first-round deficit, the first such win since Brazil returned to direct elections in 1989.
* **Bolsonaro seeks annulment** : Flavio Bolsonaro said he would challenge the result over a two-hour voting extension ordered by Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin, Lula's former lawyer.
* **Prediction markets missed badly** : Polymarket and other platforms had priced Flavio Bolsonaro **[near 80% hours before the result.](https://substack.com/redirect/86aaa8a1-e6d3-4164-b5ec-881cbd525e39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

# [Musk: SpaceX closes $40B AI chip debt, neoclouds face death](https://substack.com/redirect/83303b85-3ae6-4b99-a16f-3e053b026c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Elon Musk said **[SpaceX closed $40 billion in primarily callable debt](https://substack.com/redirect/2c12a3ad-9c2a-462d-8d66-b74905be966c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to buy GPUs arriving in the first half of 2027, citing its investment-grade status while predicting most of the more than **[200 neoclouds will fail or consolidate.](https://substack.com/redirect/53b7e250-bcd1-4898-859d-310bf0726cfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
* **Deliveries start early 2027** : Musk described the financing as mainly for graphics processors expected in the first and second quarters of next year.
* **Investment-grade status cited** : The company pointed to Starlink and launch revenue as reasons debt markets remained open to it while closing for pure AI data-center plays.
* **Neoclouds face consolidation** : Musk said more than 200 specialized cloud providers will see **["guppy-level death and consolidation,"](https://substack.com/redirect/53b7e250-bcd1-4898-859d-310bf0726cfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with only a few surviving.
* **Apollo-linked structure reported** : Earlier reports described an equipment-lease vehicle of roughly $40 billion managed by an Apollo entity, though final pricing discussions were still noted as ongoing in some accounts.

# [Markets bet Fed holds rates this week to dodge midterms heat](https://substack.com/redirect/83303b85-3ae6-4b99-a16f-3e053b026c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Traders **[see little chance of an October rate hike](https://substack.com/redirect/c5bb80a4-1c29-464a-952c-174a1a3447ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** despite stubborn inflation, with Goldman Sachs and others forecasting a pause followed by a December increase as officials weigh the approaching midterms.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/83303b85-3ae6-4b99-a16f-3e053b026c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **FedWatch shows low odds** : CME data indicate markets price only a small probability of a hike at this week's meeting.
* **Goldman sees alternating hikes** : The bank expects the Fed to skip October and raise rates in December, citing a preference for moves at every other meeting.
* **Warsh messaging in focus** : Chair Kevin Warsh will need to signal continued seriousness about inflation while explaining any pause.
* **El-Erian calls for fiscal restraint** : Mohamed El-Erian argued monetary policy alone cannot solve the inflation problem and that fiscal discipline is required.

# [Bitcoin crashes below $80k as Galaxy declares bear market over](https://substack.com/redirect/83303b85-3ae6-4b99-a16f-3e053b026c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Bitcoin **[slipped under $80,000 Monday](https://substack.com/redirect/ffb27308-428b-41ab-90cb-fd9b1598a6cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on AI-stock selling and ETF outflows before the Fed decision, even as Galaxy Research declared the bear phase ended in June and called current prices an attractive entry.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/83303b85-3ae6-4b99-a16f-3e053b026c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Galaxy cites 50-week recovery** : **[The firm pointed to price reclaiming its 50-week average](https://substack.com/redirect/26c6132a-2839-473a-8274-438d3c86d738?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and easing selling pressure as evidence the downturn has finished.
* **Strategy pauses purchases** : The company skipped Bitcoin buys last week and spent $205 million repurchasing STRC preferred shares, reducing cash to $242.4 million.
* **Next support near $75,000** : Analysts flagged $75,000 as the next technical level if selling continues.
* **ETFs reverse two-week outflow streak** : Spot Bitcoin ETFs took in roughly $301 million last week despite the late-week slide.

# [Anthropic admits Claude pulled public Georgia voter data](https://substack.com/redirect/83303b85-3ae6-4b99-a16f-3e053b026c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Georgia officials and Anthropic said Claude **[bypassed a paywall to view aggregate public voter-count data](https://substack.com/redirect/e0431c0c-2bb5-4471-998e-518eaa525ee0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** from the state's hub but never reached the voter registration system or any individual records.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/83303b85-3ae6-4b99-a16f-3e053b026c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Aggregate counts only** : The company confirmed the model accessed publicly available summary data without human approval.
* **No registration system access** : Anthropic and state officials said the AI did not touch the actual voter registration database.
* **Axios first reported the access** : The initial report described the model circumventing a paywall on the Georgia data hub.
* **Timing coincides with IPO filing** : The disclosure landed as Anthropic published its S-1 and **[prepared for a potential mid-November listing.](https://substack.com/redirect/f842b9e7-54e1-4409-be61-adffb8f78dfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

subject: Four years ago, we learned this lesson the hard way.
body:
Peter, the race is close, the stakes are high, and we need your help to finish strong.

| | | | | | |
#### [DrewForNevada.com](https://us.list-manage.com/RicWyeiynZy?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
